Bahamut is an excellent patron for good-aligned groups; he's unlikely to work with evil characters unless he thinks they can be convinced to change their ways. He's likely to conceal his true nature from the characters.

items.name: Strahd von Zarovich
items.entry: Trapped in the domain of Barovia, the vampire {@book Strahd|XDMG|8|Strahd von Zarovich} is described in {@book Ravenloft: The Horrors Within|RHW} and {@adventure Curse of Strahd|CoS}. Strahd wields supreme power in his homeland, but he can't leave it. He needs the characters to be his eyes and ears outside Barovia. Supremely egotistical, Strahd finds the idea of concealing his true identity entertaining for a while, but once the party has done a task or two for him, the mask comes off and the vampire reveals himself. Knowingly working with Strahd for an extended time likely won't appeal to most heroic parties, though Strahd could make a great ongoing patron for amoral adventurers.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Magical Entity
entries: Instead of using one of the magical entities described above, you can create an entity to serve as a group patron for your characters. You might start by skimming through the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} looking for intelligent monsters with a CR of 13 or higher.

Even if your magical entity is frightening, strange, or otherworldly, that doesn't mean the entity must be evil. Creatures commonly associated with evil deeds—such as chromatic dragons or undead—might have a change of heart and shift to a neutral or good alignment. But even a good magical entity can come across as weird, remote, or unsettling. Ordinary folk flee from the entity, but the characters are brave enough to interact with them.
When you create a magical entity for your campaign, you can roll on or choose from the Magical Entity Type table to determine the entity's nature.

entries.caption: Magical Entity Type
rows: Angel. This powerful Celestial from the Upper Planes disguises itself to mingle among ordinary people and seeks virtuous characters to join its fight against evil.

Beast Lord. An immortal, legendary spirit in animal form, such as an {@creature Animal Lord|XMM}, protects the environment and its inhabitants. The spirit needs emissaries as well as strike teams to combat threats to the land.
Ancient Dragon. A chromatic dragon who has turned away from evil behavior or a metallic dragon who champions good recruits the characters for their valiant heroics.

Giant. A {@creature Storm Giant|XMM} leader who lives in a flying castle high above the realm, hidden by clouds or a perpetual storm, has a vested interest in matters on the ground and sponsors the characters to act as the giant's emissary.
Reformed Rakshasa. A Lawful Good {@creature Rakshasa|XMM} works layered schemes against other Fiends and recruits the characters to further its mission.
Undying Steward. A powerful mage helped found the realm and is thought long dead, but they have survived as a {@creature Baelnorn|AU} or a {@creature Taisus|AU} (see {@book chapter 6|AU|6} for both).

entries.name: Magical Entity Patron Perks
entries: Characters in a party whose patron is a magical entity gain the following perks.

entries.name: Compensation
entries: The magical entity pays for the work you do on their behalf. For every mission you successfully perform for the entity, you are rewarded with treasure worth 250 GP (or more, at the DM's discretion). Your patron might reward you with Common or Uncommon magic items, especially consumables such as potions and {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls}.

entries.name: Friends in Strange Places
entries: Monsters of the same creature type as the magical entity are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you by default.

entries.name: Name Drop
entries: You can reveal the name of your group patron to your enemies, filling them with trepidation. When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check to influence a creature, you can name your group patron, granting you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check. If that check succeeds, you then gain a bonus to all checks made to influence that creature for 1 hour; the bonus is equal to half your level. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until 7 days have passed.

entries.name: Magical Entity Contacts
entries: A magical entity is typically reclusive. Their unusual appearance and nature mean that they can't simply walk down the streets of a settlement or meet the characters in a tavern—at least, not without an excellent disguise. For this reason, a magical entity is likely to communicate with the party through an intermediary or magical effect. But these contacts and effects, like the entity, should be unsettling or even scary.
Roll on or choose from the Magical Entity Contact table to determine how the magical entity interacts with the characters.

entries.caption: Magical Entity Contact
rows: Awakened Beasts. One or more awakened Beasts deliver the details of the characters' missions. The characters might consistently meet with an awakened Beast quest giver, or they might receive each quest from a different creature.
Enigmatic Dreams. The entity communicates with the characters through the {@spell Dream|XPHB} spell, sending them strange dreams suggesting specific courses of action.
Lackey. A {@creature Commoner|XMM} servant attends the entity and delivers messages to the characters along with dire warnings of the consequences of failure.

Mirror Reflections. The entity communicates to the characters via mirrors using illusions. The entity appears as the reflection of one of the characters, or the entity's image replaces that of a character.
Prophecy. The entity communicates indirectly by spreading prophecies to those nearby. The characters are expected to undertake missions that would fulfill the prophecies.

Shape-Shifter. The entity never openly appears to the characters, but creatures that claim to be the entity's servants deliver the characters' assignments. These creatures are the entity in disguise, using the {@spell Shapechange|XPHB} spell or a similar ability.

entries.name: A Magical Entity Campaign
entries: A campaign driven by a magical entity patron might unfold according to this outline:

items.name: Levels 1–4
items.entry: The campaign begins as the characters stumble into the entity's domain and prove themselves against creatures the entity considers enemies. Aberrations such as {@creature Grell|XMM|Grells}, {@creature Grick|XMM|Gricks}, and {@creature Grimlock|XMM|Grimlocks} are all thematically appropriate foes.

items.name: Levels 5–10
items.entry: The magical entity approaches the characters or invites them to the entity's lair and offers to become their group patron, sending them on missions against monstrous foes. Githyanki and slaadi make good antagonists for this tier of play.

items.name: Levels 11–16
items.entry: The mysterious mastermind controlling these Aberrations—whom the characters haven't yet identified—captures or imprisons the magical entity, perhaps through the use of an Artifact, and the characters must rescue them. The characters battle {@creature Aboleth|XMM|Aboleths}, {@creature Beholder|XMM|Beholders}, {@creature Death Tyrant|XMM|Death Tyrants}, and {@creature Mind Flayer Arcanist|XMM|Mind Flayer Arcanists}.

items.name: Levels 17–20
items.entry: The mysterious mastermind is revealed as a creature similar to the group patron, but different in nature. For example, Bahamut is captured by a group of {@creature Ancient Red Dragon|XMM|Ancient Red Dragons}. Or Strahd is at the mercy of a powerful {@creature Lich|XMM}, such as Acererak or Vecna. These two liches are further described in {@adventure Vecna: Eve of Ruin|VEoR}, including game statistics for Vecna.

entries.name: Political Faction
entries: A political faction group patron is tied to the governing structure of a magical realm. A political faction usually has great wealth and access to the realm's resources, but the faction leaders are politicians and bureaucrats, not adventurers. Even if the leaders are powerful mages, they have no interest in risking their own lives. Instead, they hire the characters as spies or agents.

Campaigns with a political faction group patron combine high magic with political intrigue. The characters might be kept in the dark by their patron faction, which gives them only the information they absolutely need (and sometimes not even that). The faction sends the party into dangerous situations that force them to improvise.

entries.name: Political Faction Motivations
entries: A political faction might patronize a group for the following reasons:

items.name: The Characters Are Residents
items.entry: If the characters live in the realm where the faction governs, the faction believes the characters are easier to recruit and more likely to be loyal. The faction might exert legal pressure on the characters, forcing them to do as the faction requires.

items.name: The Characters Are Foreign
items.entry: The faction prefers to hire outsiders who can operate in neighboring realms without attracting attention, and who know the languages and customs of the faction's rivals.

items.name: The Characters Are Deniable Assets
items.entry: The political faction hires the adventures without official sanction. The party is sent on dangerous missions in far-off lands, and if they're captured, the political faction denies any connection or responsibility for the party's actions.

entries.name: Political Faction Patrons

entries.title: The Red Wizards of Thay are a dangerous and powerful group patron.

entries: The following organizations, each detailed in {@book Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn|FRHoF}, could serve as political faction group patrons:

items.name: Red Wizards
items.entry: The Red Wizards rule Thay, a land on the eastern edge of Faerûn in the Forgotten Realms. Thay is expansionist, and its rulers are mostly cruel tyrants. Thay and the Red Wizards are expanded on in {@adventure Arcana Unleashed: Deadfall|AUD}, which includes an adventure that embroils characters in a mission to kill {@book Szass Tam|XDMG|8|Szass Tam}, a Red Wizard lich who plots to once again control the nation.

items.name: Simbarch Council
items.entry: Thay's neighbor, the land of Aglarond, is ruled by a group of sorcerers called the Simbarch Council. In addition to governing the realm, the council trains sorcerers who come to Aglarond from across Faerûn. Aglarond has a long history of military conflict with Thay.

items.name: Witches of Rashemen
items.entry: Rashemen is a land on Thay's northern border. Rashemen is ruled by masked warlocks known as wychlaren, who make pacts with ancient spirits that dwell in Rashemen's dense and magical forests. Like Aglarond, Rashemen has been invaded repeatedly by Thay, and some of the witches occasionally wish to strike at their longtime enemies.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Political Faction
entries: Instead of using one of the political factions described above, you can create a political faction to serve as a group patron for your characters.

Political factions have a long history in the realms where they appear, and they're distinguished by symbols, mottoes, and pass phrases. They require an oath, though some members of the faction are more loyal to that oath than others. Give some thought to the faction's history and how its fortunes have risen or fallen over time. Give your faction at least one rival group in the same realm or a neighboring one; many adventures the characters undertake should be missions against a rival.
When you create a political faction for your campaign, you can roll on or choose from the Political Faction Type table to determine the faction's nature.

entries.caption: Political Faction Type
rows: Environmentalists. The faction seeks to magically preserve the realm's natural spaces and wildlife. It doesn't receive funding and resources from the government, so it recruits the characters to act as its agents.
Magical Intelligence Agency. This government agency, which protects the realm from magical threats, needs the characters to investigate cases and neutralize dangers.
Magical Military. The characters are soldiers in the realm's army. They're given orders by individuals of higher rank who expect to be obeyed.

Rebel Faction. The faction opposes the current rulers of the realm and operates from a secret base. The characters are tasked with gathering resources and allies for a coming revolt, though if the characters are caught, the rebels disavow all knowledge of them.
Ruling Party. The faction is in power due to its members' magical prowess. The faction needs the characters to sniff out threats to ensure the nation's safety—and the faction's political supremacy.
Shadow Cabinet. The shadow cabinet operates clandestinely. The characters know the truth and must keep their missions secret lest the rulers discover and disband the faction.

entries.name: Political Faction Patron Perks
entries: Characters in a party whose patron is a political faction gain the following perks.

entries.name: Expenses and Salary
entries: Your patron reimburses you for expenses incurred as part of your work. You are required to account for your expenses and must explain any extraordinary expenditures, but routine travel, ordinary equipment, and basic services don't draw a second glance.

Additionally, your employment brings an income of 1 GP per day (enough to sustain a {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle). At the DM's discretion, your salary might increase or decrease depending on the faction's nature, the type of work, and the length of your employment.

entries.name: Immunity
entries: As long as you remain in the political faction's good graces, you can avoid prosecution for minor offenses under the laws of the realm where the faction is based. However, committing serious crimes, especially if they're unrelated to assigned work, is a sure way to fall out of your patron's good graces.

entries.name: Powerful Allies
entries: The political faction has secured alliances with powerful businesspeople, spellcasters, and tradespeople. The faction can call upon these allies to secure transportation for you by a means of your choosing (via coach, ship, or teleportation) at half the usual cost. When you take a Bastion turn, if you are level 9+, you can (as a group) issue the Recruit order to the political faction as if the faction was a {@facility Teleportation Circle|XDMG} facility in your Bastion. If you are level 17+, you can instead issue the Recruit order to the political faction as if it were a {@facility Guildhall|XDMG} facility within your Bastion.

entries.name: Political Faction Contacts
entries: A political faction has well-established procedures establishing how the characters communicate with their superiors, get to adventure sites, and return home when the mission is over. Procedures include rules for disguising communications, such as leaving messages in dead drops or protecting reports with the {@spell Illusory Script|XPHB} spell.

A political faction is large enough to include a cast of recurring characters, and the party might have a different contact for every mission. Alternatively, the party's contact might change when a shift in government or evolving political philosophy forces the faction to adapt.
Roll on or choose from the Political Faction Contact table to determine who manages the relationship between the characters and the political faction.

entries.caption: Political Faction Contact
rows: Excitable Artificer. The contact is eager for the characters to test their latest inventions—which are often unsafe.
Harried Bureaucrat. This administrator has a busy schedule and lacks the time or resources to supervise every task. They assign missions in a rush and leave the party to sort out the details.
Naive Intellectual. This reclusive intellectual with encyclopedic knowledge but no field expertise suggests impractical or unrealistic courses of action.
Political Officer. Responsible for prioritizing the faction's political agenda, the officer frequently questions the characters' loyalty.
Public Relations Expert. The contact magically manipulates public perception and strives to make the characters popular.
Well-Mannered Aristocrat. This genteel individual personally meets with the characters to give them their missions, usually over tea in their magic-filled abode.

entries.name: A Political Faction Campaign
entries: A campaign driven by a political faction patron might unfold according to this outline:

items.name: Levels 1–4
items.entry: The characters are recruited by intermediaries and are unaware they're serving the political faction. They receive a mission to infiltrate a rival faction and steal the spellbook of a well-protected {@creature Mage|XMM}.

items.name: Levels 5–10
items.entry: Having proven themselves, the characters are brought further into the faction and learn their employer's identity. New missions send them to rival nations, where they sabotage rituals, steal magic items, plant incriminating evidence, and thwart plots to assassinate members of their patron faction.

items.name: Levels 11–16
items.entry: The characters learn about a plot by a rival faction to assemble or retrieve an Artifact capable of great destruction in the realm where the patron faction is based. Retrieving and destroying the Artifact leads the characters on a grand adventure that visits multiple planes of existence.

items.name: Levels 17–20
items.entry: A sudden and overwhelming strike by a rival faction eliminates most of the highest-ranking members of the patron faction, and the characters ascend into those positions. Now they must decide how to respond to the attack and settle the rivalry once and for all.

entries.name: Trickster
entries: Tricksters are powerful beings—often archfey—who are known for their whimsical nature. A trickster can take many forms and might appear pleasant, angry, or simply otherworldly. But at their core, the trickster is unpredictable, their priorities and goals changing with the seasons or even from day to day.

Tricksters make good patrons for groups that prefer social interaction, exploration, and nonviolent conflict resolution over combat. Many tricksters prefer humiliating and pranking their enemies to killing them. Groups with a trickster patron are likely to spend time in the {@book Feywild|XDMG|5|Feywild}, visiting Domains of Delight and learning the distinctive rules of each.

entries.name: Trickster Motivations
entries: A trickster might patronize a group for the following reasons:

items.name: The Characters Are Interesting
items.entry: Tricksters are like magpies, driven to collect shiny baubles. Adventurers are colorful, larger-than-life personalities who are likely to attract a trickster's attention.

items.name: The Trickster Needs Plausible Deniability
items.entry: A trickster makes enemies, and those enemies often instantly recognize the trickster and are alert to disguises. The trickster needs agents who aren't known to be associated with the trickster.

items.name: The Characters Are Expendable Assets
items.entry: The trickster needs dangerous tasks accomplished and is unwilling to send their more experienced agents out of concern those agents might not return. The characters' deaths won't inconvenience the trickster.

entries.title: Tasha is a trickster patron whose myriad alliances shroud her motivations in mystery.

entries.name: Trickster Patrons
entries: The following characters from the D&D multiverse, all briefly described in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}, could serve as trickster patrons:

items.name: Queen of Air and Darkness
items.entry: The Queen of Air and Darkness is a foreboding and mysterious archfey who rules the Gloaming Court, a Domain of Delight in the {@book Feywild|XDMG|5|Feywild}. She favors followers who are willful and follow their instincts, obeying no laws. She's likely to give the characters total freedom to choose how to accomplish their missions.

items.name: Summer Queen
items.entry: Titania, the Summer Queen, is a benevolent figure, but she nonetheless displays all the whimsical arbitrariness of other archfey. The Summer Court is infamous for its elaborate rules of behavior; characters working for Titania inevitably break unstated rules, prompting Titania to assign them punishments that lead to further adventures.

items.name: Tasha
items.entry: {@book Tasha|XDMG|8|Tasha}, the adopted daughter of Baba Yaga, is a mighty spellcaster who authored the {@i Demonomicon} and invented several famous spells. Tasha has a unique relationship with fate, having been a tyrant known as Iggwilv, the Witch Queen of Perrenland; a planes-walking archmage; and Zybilna, archfey of the domain of Prismeer. You can learn more about Tasha in {@adventure The Wild Beyond the Witchlight|WBtW}. Her mysterious goals could lead the characters anywhere in the multiverse.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Trickster
entries: Instead of using one of the tricksters described above, you can create a trickster to serve as a group patron for your characters.

A trickster group patron is whimsical, entertaining, and funny. However, a little whimsy goes a long way. Your trickster should focus their practical jokes and pranks on rivals and enemies, not the characters, or the party will soon find the trickster tiresome rather than amusing. Ensure that the trickster (mostly) tells the truth to the characters while maintaining a sense of humor and indulging the characters' pranks and jests.
When you create a trickster for your campaign, you can roll on or choose from the Trickster Type table to determine their nature.

entries.caption: Trickster Type
rows: Bored Immortal. This being has lived for centuries or perhaps millennia and has seen it all. They desperately crave entertainment and generously pay anyone who provides spectacle—the more dangerous, the better.

Child Prodigy. A young child of incredibly powerful magical beings, the prodigy has inherited great power but doesn't yet have the maturity to use it wisely. The prodigy uses their force of will and considerable monetary resources to convince the characters to undertake their capricious missions.
God of Mischief. A god devoted to mischief and deception conceals their identity from the party while sending the characters on missions to humiliate the god's rivals.

Long-Forgotten {@creature Archmage|XMM}. This ancient archmage, long thought dead, possesses great power but is increasingly eccentric and bitter that no one remembers their most glorious past deeds. The archmage hires the characters to fool individuals from the archmage's past into making amends for perceived misdeeds.

Puckish Fey. This powerful fey serves the archfey ruler of a Domain of Delight as a court jester or is themself an archfey. The fey delights in sending the characters on well-paid missions that further the trickster's schemes or simply amuse them.
Willful Hag. A hag coven member doesn't approve of deeds performed by the other hags in the coven and assigns the characters missions to secretly undermine the rival hags.

entries.name: Trickster Patron Perks
entries: Characters in a party whose patron is a trickster gain the following perks.

entries.name: Compensation
entries: A trickster group patron pays you as a way of binding you to them and ensuring your continued loyalty. On average, the trickster pays each member of your group 4 GP per day (enough to sustain a {@book Wealthy|XPHB|6|Wealthy (4 GP per Day)} lifestyle). They might bestow additional gifts such as gemstones, art objects, or Common or Uncommon magic items on you on completion of a successful mission. However, the trickster might withhold this money and reclaim gifts if you displease them or refuse an onerous mission.

entries.name: Fickle Friends
entries: The trickster has formed many surprising relationships in their travels across the multiverse, and they can call upon unexpected allies to aid your missions. These allies are often otherworldly—including devils, demons, fey, and stranger creatures—but they are always {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} while aiding you (though not necessarily afterward). The trickster can call on these friends to secure transportation for you by a means of your choosing (via coach, ship, or teleportation) at half the usual cost. When you take a Bastion turn, if you are level 9+, you can (as a group) issue the Recruit order to the trickster as if they were a {@facility Teleportation Circle|XDMG} facility in your Bastion.

entries.name: Resources
entries: The trickster has a vast collection of dangerous relics, magic items, spellbooks, and other resources collected over a long lifetime. You can call in a favor to gain access to these resources. Additionally, you can consult with the trickster or their more powerful associates, if you're willing to risk their attention.

entries.name: Strange Gifts
entries: The trickster grants your group a small measure of esoteric power. At level 5, and again at level 13, you each gain one {@filter supernatural gift|rewards|type=blessing;charm} as described in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}. The DM determines which supernatural gifts are available.

entries.name: Trickster Contacts
entries: {@skill Deception|XPHB} is key to the trickster group patron, and a trickster is likely to meet with the characters personally while concealing their identity. But not all tricksters can disguise themselves, and the disguise falls away once the trickster finds the joke has worn stale. Tricksters instead might communicate with the characters through various other means, including agents, spells, or magic items.
If the trickster uses an agent, roll on or choose from the Trickster Contact table to determine who manages the relationship between the characters and the trickster.

entries.caption: Trickster Contact
rows: Bound by Debt. A creature the trickster saved from a terrible fate brings the characters messages to work off the debt incurred by this rescue.
Bound Demon. A demon the trickster bound long ago is magically prevented from doing evil and satisfies itself with pranking the party and encouraging them to solve problems with violence.

Faerie Dragon. The trickster's {@creature Faerie Dragon Youth|XMM} attendant occasionally slips away to give advice and gifts to the characters. The trickster might be unaware of the faerie dragon's mercurial actions.

Minuscule Fey. The contact, a {@creature Pixie|XMM} or {@creature Sprite|XMM}, is desperately in love with the trickster and considers the party to be the means by which the contact can earn the trickster's affection.

Transformed Enemy. The trickster overcame a hated rival long ago and transformed the rival into a sentient magic item, a talking animal, or another form. Now the rival delivers messages to the party and warns them against the trickster.
Wise Centaur. This wise, patient, and elderly {@creature Centaur Warden|XMM} has trained generations of adventurers. The centaur doesn't always agree with the trickster but respects their power.

entries.name: A Trickster Campaign
entries: A campaign driven by a trickster patron might unfold according to this outline:

items.name: Levels 1–4
items.entry: The trickster recruits the characters while concealing their own identity and tests the characters by pitting them against lesser Fey such as {@filter bullywugs|bestiary|group=bullywugs}, {@filter goblins|bestiary|group=goblinoids}, and {@creature Worg|XMM|worgs} in service to a coven of {@creature Green Hag|XMM|Green Hags}.

items.name: Levels 5–10
items.entry: The characters have earned the grudging respect of the trickster, who sends them into the Feywild on missions that emphasize exploration and interaction. The party is tasked with stealing a bauble the trickster favors or persuading two of the trickster's enemies to fight each other.

items.name: Levels 11–16
items.entry: The trickster's enemies catch up with them, and the characters must protect their patron from demons, adult dragons, and mortal archmages, all of whom have longstanding grudges against the trickster.

items.name: Levels 17–20
items.entry: The characters discover the enemies fighting the trickster are being subtly manipulated by a villainous {@creature Arch-hag|XMM} that seeks to supplant the trickster and seize their role. To end the threat, the characters must corner the hag in its lair.

entries.name: Wizards' Circle
entries: Powerful spellcasters occasionally form an alliance known as a wizards' circle to pursue goals beyond the reach of any individual. Wizards' circles are often temporary, formed to resolve a specific problem that threatens the world or the multiverse. But even archmages need friends or allies, and the members of a wizards' circle might make their alliance permanent.

In many ways, a wizards' circle is like an archmage group patron, with the added complication that the circle consists of several strong-willed individuals who don't necessarily like each other. The characters get caught in the middle of long debates and old rivalries between members of the circle, and it can be hard to satisfy one member of the circle without alienating another.

entries.name: Wizards' Circle Motivations
entries: A wizards' circle might patronize a group for the following reasons:

items.name: The Characters Balance Each Other
items.entry: Each member of the wizards' circle has their own preferences when selecting agents and operatives. The party represents a collection of these preferences, with each member of the circle backing one member of the party. Although each character is backed by a single member, the circle as a whole serves as a group patron for the characters.

items.name: The Characters Have Special Skills
items.entry: A wizards' circle lacks expertise in fields outside members' specialties, including types of magic outside their bailiwick, martial prowess, or exploration skills. The characters provide useful abilities that the circle members lack.

items.name: Pawns on the Chessboard
items.entry: The wizards' circle supports the group because the characters feature in the circle's long-term plans. The circle members might know one of the characters is unknowingly a noble and thus a potential candidate for the throne, or they might have identified one of the characters as the only person who can safely wield a dangerous Artifact. These facts might not be known to the characters.

entries.title: Notoriously argumentative mages Jallarzi Sallavarian, Bigby, and Mordenkainen unite when a dire threat to their world arises.

entries.name: Wizards' Circle Patrons
entries: The following organizations could serve as wizards' circle group patrons:

items.name: Circle of Eight
items.entry: The Circle of Eight is an alliance of powerful spellcasters that includes the gnome {@book Bigby|XDMG|8|Bigby}; the humans {@book Jallarzi Sallavarian|XDMG|8|Jallarzi Sallavarian}, {@book Mordenkainen|XDMG|8|Mordenkainen}, and {@book Otiluke|XDMG|8|Otiluke}; and the dwarf {@book Otto|XDMG|8|Otto}, all briefly described in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}. The Circle is based in the world of Greyhawk and concerns itself with maintaining the power balance between Oerth's realms and factions. The Circle of Eight favors neutral-aligned agents and avoids attention, preferring to work behind the scenes.

items.name: Order of the Many-Starred Cloak
items.entry: The Order of the Many-Starred Cloak is dedicated to defending and supporting Neverwinter, a city in the Forgotten Realms. In the past, the order has protected the city from rival mages in nearby Luskan, among other threats. Members include powerful mages such as the human Gallio Elibro, who's known for his planar research. The order might hire characters to investigate threats against the city, such as monsters amassed near Neverwinter or cults ensconced in the city.

items.name: Wizards Three
items.entry: The wizard Alustriel Silverhand called on her friends Tasha and Mordenkainen to thwart one of Vecna's plots. This alliance is known as the Wizards Three, and it is detailed in {@adventure Vecna: Eve of Ruin|VEoR}. In that adventure, one of the Wizards Three isn't who they appear to be; you might continue this deception or decide the three wizards continue their alliance once Vecna is defeated.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Wizards' Circle
entries: Instead of using one of the wizards' circles described above, you can create a wizards' circle to serve as a group patron for your characters. You can use several of the archmage stat blocks in {@book chapter 6|AU|6}, each of which specializes in one school of magic. If your world has a mages' guild, discussed earlier in this chapter, that guild might make an excellent wizards' circle group patron.

To make your own wizards' circle, start by creating one circle member for each of the player characters; this member acts as a personal patron to that character, while the circle as a whole supports the party's activities. For example, if one of your players has created a Sorcerer with the Draconic Sorcery subclass, the circle might include a dragon who has chosen the sorcerer as their personal agent. Other circle members, however, support different characters, and these members are the dragon's rivals.
When you create a wizards' circle for your campaign, you can roll on or choose from the Wizards' Circle Type table.

entries.caption: Wizards' Circle Type
rows: Council of the Wise. The circle members are the world's mightiest, most benevolent mages, but the most charismatic of them is secretly a traitor. Most of the characters' missions are altruistic, but occasionally the traitor sends them on missions meant to sow discord among the group.

Disaster Preventers. The circle members don't like each other, but they've come together to stop the apocalypse. They need the characters to achieve lesser missions while they focus on the larger threat.

Grudging Allies. Longtime enemies, the circle members wreaked great destruction during their conflicts. They've agreed to avoid fighting each other, instead using the characters to pursue the goals they can agree on.
Pub Crew. The circle formed as an excuse to drink and socialize. Members have no time for dangerous missions to save the world, sending the characters instead.
War Veterans. The circle members are veterans who have served together in several wars. In their retirement, they prefer to send more energetic operatives—the characters—to stop the next great war.

Well-Meaning Imposters. The circle members are frauds with only minor magical power. They maintain this ruse because without the circle, the realm would collapse into warring factions. If the characters learn of the wizards' lack of ability, they might continue to work for the circle to avoid larger conflicts.

entries.name: Wizards' Circle Patron Perks
entries: Characters in a party whose patron is a wizards' circle gain the following perks.

entries.name: Assisting Apprentices
entries: The wizards in the circle have trained numerous apprentices, many of whom are loyal to their mentor. Whenever you're in a city, a former apprentice of a circle member can cast any level 1 or lower spell at no cost, as long as you identify yourself as an agent of that circle member. A former apprentice can cast any level 2–8 spell for you at half the usual cost, as long as you're in a city and similarly identify yourself.

entries.name: Compensation
entries: The wizards' circle pays you to complete tasks on the circle's behalf. On average, the wizards' circle pays each member of your group 2 GP per day (enough to sustain a {@book Comfortable|XPHB|6|Comfortable (2 GP per Day)} lifestyle). Or you might be paid (at least 300 GP) after completing each task the wizards' circle assigns.

entries.name: Magical Resources
entries: The wizards' circle has collected untold magic items and magical curiosities. This collection is scattered among the sanctums of the circle members. A wizards' circle can give members of the group any Common or Uncommon magic item in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}, as long as possession of the item would help the group's tasks. When the characters reach level 11, the wizards' circle can retrieve one Rare and one Very Rare magic item in between the group's tasks and award it to them as additional compensation. When the characters reach level 17, the wizards' circle can retrieve one Rare, Very Rare, or Legendary magic item in between tasks and award it to the group as additional compensation.

entries.name: Safe Houses
entries: The wizards' circle maintains magically warded safe houses and hiding spots throughout the world or across multiple worlds. Your group knows how to locate these hidden redoubts and can sustain a {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle in one for no cost. Revealing the location of one of these safe houses, whether purposefully or by accident, causes you to lose favor with the wizards' circle, and you might be banned from using them.

entries.name: Wizards' Circle Contacts
entries: The members of a wizards' circle don't always agree, and they keep secrets from each other. An individual in the circle might meet with only one or two characters at a time, in secret. In addition, the circle as a whole has an official spokesperson who communicates with the characters and gives them tasks.
Roll on or choose from the Wizards' Circle Contact table to determine who manages the relationship between the characters and the wizards' circle.

entries.caption: Wizards' Circle Contact
rows: Abjurer. Specializing in healing and protective magic, the contact wards the characters before adventures, heals them afterward, and urges the characters to be cautious.
Conjurer. The contact specializes in teleportation magic and summoning magical allies. If the party is in great danger, the contact teleports them to safety or sends magical creations to help.
Diviner. Before every mission, the contact delivers enigmatic advice that the characters find useful—if they can decipher its meaning and recall it at the right moment.
Evoker. This evoker proposes the most direct and destructive way to solve any problem. They don't worry about collateral damage incurred during a mission.

Illusionist. The characters know little about the contact, not even their true appearance or identity. The contact could show up in any context or situation, even appearing to be someone else whom the party knows well.

Necromancer. The contact ghoulishly asks the characters to bring back corpses or body parts from their adventures but is willing to cast the {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB} spell if a character perishes on a mission.

entries.name: A Wizards' Circle Campaign
entries: A campaign driven by a wizards' circle patron might unfold according to this outline:

items.name: Levels 1–4
items.entry: Each character in the group is selected by a single member of the wizards' circle and brought together to serve the circle. Early missions pit the group against opposing {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM|Mage Apprentices}, {@creature Nothic|XMM|Nothics}, and other magical threats.

items.name: Levels 5–10
items.entry: When the characters seek to recover magical lore, obtain dangerous Artifacts, or slay magical foes, sometimes the object of their quest is missing or has already fled. It slowly becomes clear that someone inside the circle is feeding information to the circle's enemies.

items.name: Levels 11–16
items.entry: The traitorous member of the circle reveals themself and seizes control of the circle and its resources. Other members of the circle are imprisoned, slain, bought off, or cowed into working with the traitor. The characters might play along for a while or go on the run, but eventually they must confront the traitor and their allies.

items.name: Levels 17–20
items.entry: Now that the traitorous member of the circle is dealt with, the circle has openings for new members. The characters join the circle, recruiting new agents and rounding up the traitor's remaining followers.

data.name: Chapter 4: Magical Factions

entries.title: Mages engage in a magical duel while members of the Crucible Keepers look on.

entries: Many scholars and practitioners of magic seek ever-greater prowess and status, but few can achieve these individually. Instead, those pursuing mystical knowledge often join influential groups. Numerous in membership and great in achievement, these factions accept adventurers into their folds, offering resources and knowledge in exchange for loyalty and service.

Each faction described in this chapter has its own outlook and goals, such as providing magical advice and entertainment to influence the powerful, researching alien forces from beyond the stars, and uncovering the secrets of life and undeath.

Faction members exchange magical discoveries, mentor pupils, and learn from more experienced colleagues. Members are united by shared specialties and philosophies. Although these organizations' disparate objectives often bring them into conflict with each other, members of different factions might also unite over common goals.
You can use these factions as patrons, as villains, or as organizations the characters can join. Adapt them to your world or campaign as needed.

entries.name: Faction Descriptions
entries: This chapter includes details on the following factions:

items: {@area Bejeweled Conclave.|1c8|x} The discreet enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave make themselves invaluable to powerful clients as elite entertainers, advisers, and mediators while amassing clients' secrets.
{@area Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.|1d8|x} Reclusive transmuters obsessed with mutations, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn seek guidance from alien intelligences.
{@area Covenant of the Grave.|1ed|x} The necromancers of the Covenant of the Grave study death and undeath with scientific precision, seeking esoteric knowledge through rigorous research.

{@area Crucible Keepers.|201|x} From volcanic eruptions to shore-shredding hurricanes, no natural disaster is too dangerous for the daring Crucible Keepers to study in their pursuit of ever-escalating applications for Evocation magic.
{@area Horizon Weavers.|213|x} The Horizon Weavers' conjurers practice summoning and teleportation as they explore and chart the multiverse.

{@area Ninth Quill.|224|x} The spies and saboteurs of the Ninth Quill steal lore and artifacts from other powerful mages; many members do so to safeguard these treasures, but others are motivated by greed. The Ninth Quill also stokes dissent among the other factions to keep them from growing too powerful.
{@area Phantasmic Circus.|239|x} The showy illusionists of the Phantasmic Circus entertain eager audiences with impossible spectacles.
{@area Seers of Sea and Sky.|24c|x} The diligent oracles of the Seers of Sea and Sky divine truths in the movements of the wind and waves.
{@area Sheltering Hands.|261|x} The abjurers of the Sheltering Hands uplift the downtrodden and protect those in need.

entries.name: Magical Specializations
entries: With the exception of the Ninth Quill, each of these magical factions specializes in a particular school of magic, as shown in the Factions by School table. Ninth Quill members instead dabble in all disciplines. These specializations are as much philosophical as technical. For instance, the fireball-throwing evokers of the Crucible Keepers are often forceful personalities who enjoy dramatic displays of destructive magic. In contrast, the subtle enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave prefer to use smooth words to achieve their goals.

entries.name: Spellcasting Services
entries: Magical factions include spellcasters who specialize in the associated school of magic. A faction's base of operations counts as a city for the purpose of purchasing spellcasting services (described in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}) for spells of the associated school. At your discretion, the casting of spells that belong to other schools might also be available for purchase, and faction members might offer discounts based on the characters' relationship with the faction.

entries.name: Renown
entries: Characters can undertake missions and do favors for a faction and thereby earn renown with that faction without necessarily becoming members of the organization. Each faction description in this chapter includes benefits characters gain from accruing renown with the faction (as detailed in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|2|Renown}).

entries.name: Joining Factions
entries: Although most members of magical factions are spellcasters, characters of any class can find a home in one or more of these factions. Each description includes the process for becoming a member of the faction; the benefits for doing so; and recommendations for classes, backgrounds, and proficiencies that make characters particularly well suited to the faction. The Factions by Class table provides a summary of which factions are a good fit for each class from the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB|3}.

entries.name: Special Facilities
entries: Each faction detailed in this chapter includes a special facility that members of that faction can add to their Bastions. The rules for Bastions appear in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|10}.

entries.name: Faction Relationships
entries: The Faction Attitudes table summarizes the relationships between the factions described in this chapter. Faction pairs marked with an {@i F} consider each other allies; their members have a default attitude of {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} toward one another. Pairs marked with an {@i H} consider each other rivals; their members have a default attitude of {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} toward one another. Members of factions marked with an {@i I} begin as {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} toward one another. Exceptions might exist on an individual level.

entries.name: Bejeweled Conclave
entries: The Bejeweled Conclave is known as an organization of professional entertainers and mediators who cater to wealthy clients. They host glamorous parties, serve as courtiers, broker deals, and provide entertainment for exclusive functions.

But the Bejeweled Conclave wields far more influence than its publicly known services indicate. Consummate agents behind the throne, the enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave cultivate elite connections and shift the balance of power in cities across the world.

entries.name: Goals and Activities

entries.title: This unassuming baker is, in reality, a member of the Bejeweled Conclave's Whisper Network.

entries: The Bejeweled Conclave seeks to increase its sway across the multiverse. The faction engages skilled diplomats, courtiers, and entertainers and hones their abilities. Enchanters and spies receive a more clandestine, but no less thorough, education. The conclave prizes subtlety and secrecy above all; members are taught that it's better to fail a mission and keep the conclave's secrets than to succeed at the cost of exposing the faction's true goals.

The Bejeweled Conclave operates in major cities throughout the multiverse. Distance keeps members from knowing all their peers, but the faction is quick to celebrate successes, building loyalty and camaraderie within its ranks. While all members learn conversational tricks to offer convincing praise, the compliments members bestow on each other are usually genuine.

Conclave members understand that overtly using Enchantment magic risks exposing them as more than entertainers and courtiers. If a member must modify a noble's memories or magically dominate a general, they undertake significant planning to conceal their involvement.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: More experienced members of the Bejeweled Conclave oversee operations assigned to junior members. Valuable secrets are reported through this hierarchy up to the faction's highest ranks, referred to as the Whisper Network. These leaders hoard a treasure trove of secrets; there are few facts about the movers and shakers of civilization that the Bejeweled Conclave doesn't know.

Conclave members are trusted to act alone when necessary, such as when an important client insists on hiring only a single mediator or companion. When possible, though, senior members politely request that their "junior clerks" or "associates in training" handle more workaday aspects of their affairs. Such requests, which might include subtle magical compulsion, are a ruse to bring another trained member to operate from the shadows. As a result, clients who planned to planned to hire only one member of the Bejeweled Conclave often find themselves engaging two or three.

entries.name: Whisper Network
entries: Members of the Whisper Network keep their identities private, even from their peers. The only exception is Madame Hestia Ilverne (Medium {@creature Noble Prodigy|XMM}), a courteous human Whisper Network member who heads the conclave's public-facing efforts. Rumors within the faction claim that Madame Ilverne is among the lowest ranked of the leaders, but she seems nothing but pleased with her position.

Whether members of the Whisper Network work as music instructors, clerks, dancers, or cooks, they keep an eye on all aspects of Bejeweled Conclave activities. If they have edicts or missions to impart, they do so through Madame Ilverne. When she casually mentions a task to a member with the words "The Network would prefer a favor," all comprehend the seriousness of the request.

entries.name: Lurewood Mansion
entries: A regal manor house in the garden district of a major city, Lurewood Mansion is the conclave's academy. The previous owners donated their property generations ago for unknown reasons. The manor's architecture has been adapted to include numerous salons and studies, as well as a fine kitchen.

In the studies, members of the Bejeweled Conclave learn to negotiate deals and defuse arguments. In the salons, singers, dancers, and musicians practice entertainment suitable for elevated private parties, from subdued chamber music to sensual dances to heart-wrenching ballads. New faction members take lessons here no matter how polished they are when recruited, if for no other reason than to bolster the illusion that negotiation and entertainment are the Bejeweled Conclave's prime objectives.

Beneath the mansion, a dizzying maze of chambers connected through locked doors and one-way mirrors facilitates practice in eavesdropping, lock-picking, quick changes, and stealthy escapes. Other rooms allow members to rest out of sight. The heart of the maze contains the mansion's best-kept secret: workrooms where enchanters teach apprentice mages the arts of twisting minds, magically hiding secrets, and erasing memories.

entries.name: Joining the Conclave
entries: Aspiring faction members can't join the Bejeweled Conclave by requesting admission; members inevitably deny that there are any openings in what they claim is simply a loose professional organization.

Entry is only by invitation. Senior members carefully watch entertainers and mediators who have impressive public reputations. Those who seem particularly shrewd and ambitious might receive an invitation for free training in their specialties at Lurewood Mansion, hosted by Madame Ilverne.

Once an invitee arrives, Madame Ilverne engages them in cryptic conversation. If the potential member impresses her with their poise, acumen, and discretion, she invites them to join the faction. Otherwise, she thanks them for their time and sends them on their way without ever indicating that the mansion is anything other than a professional academy.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Bejeweled Conclave by sharing valuable secrets or completing conclave missions. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bejeweled Conclave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Bejeweled Conclave Renown
rows: You can consult the Bejeweled Conclave before meeting a significant figure for the first time to learn a personal secret—humorous, embarrassing, or otherwise socially relevant—about that person.

You can stay in Lurewood Mansion or any other residence operated by the conclave, providing you a {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle for free. If you have just returned from a dangerous locale, conclave members insist you first take a bath.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bejeweled Conclave gives you one Uncommon magic item—usually a Ring or a Wondrous Item.

Your lifestyle at Lurewood Mansion or any conclave residence increases to {@book Comfortable|XPHB|6|Comfortable (2 GP per Day)}. Additionally, you can request the aid of {@dice 1d4} {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies} for a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
If you are arrested for anything short of treason in any land where the Bejeweled Conclave operates, the conclave finds a way to have your charges dismissed.
You can arrange for a meeting with Madame Hestia Ilverne. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the conclave teaches you its entrancing magic. You always have the {@spell Enthrall|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

At your instruction, one of the conclave members casts {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} (save {@dc 15}) for free on a target of your choice. You must have met or seen the target at least once within the last 30 days, and the spell is cast within 24 hours of you choosing your target. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

Members of the conclave openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Bejeweled Conclave imparts a significant secret about you that you didn't know. This secret is up to the DM and might take the form of a {@filter supernatural gift|rewards|type=blessing;charm} (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}).

entries.name: Bejeweled Conclave Characters
entries: Joining the Bejeweled Conclave is advantageous for any character with mysterious allure, regardless of whether they use magic to enchant others. Those skilled at uncovering and trading secrets are also well suited to this faction, as are entertainers who specialize in dancing, singing, or other performance arts.

The most sought-after recruits are {@class Bard|XPHB}, {@class Rogue|XPHB}, {@class Sorcerer|XPHB}, {@class Warlock|XPHB}, or {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Enchanter|Enchanter|AU} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, or {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} or who have the {@background Bejeweled Conclave Spy|AU}, {@background Entertainer|XPHB}, or {@background Noble|XPHB} background are also likely to be recruited.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Bejeweled Conclave, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Finer Things
entries: The conclave ensures its members dress well, paying you a stipend that supports your {@book Wealthy|XPHB|6|Wealthy (4 GP per Day)} lifestyle (4 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Bejeweled Conclave Trinket|AU|Bejeweled Conclave Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bejeweled Conclave.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: As well-connected spies and secret keepers, members of the Bejeweled Conclave can provide characters with useful information. For example, the conclave might help the characters if they've lost a lead or are having trouble gaining access to an important public figure. The conclave might insist on a favor or secret in return, pulling the characters into its webs of intrigue.
The style of the Bejeweled Conclave involves elegance, manners, and class: all techniques to be admired. Just beware members' hidden agendas.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Bejeweled Conclave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn

entries.title: A member of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn transforms a colleague into a strange creature.

entries: A secretive organization of amoral transmuters, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives abstruse directives from alien entities that hail from the dark spaces between stars. Faction members magically mutate plants and creatures in preparation for visitation by these beings—an event they believe is inevitable. They believe these entities will witness their glorious transmutations, be impressed, and bring about an exalted future full of mutated aberrations that serve transmuters' every whim.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: The exact goals of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are inscrutable to many members, though all believe they are helping to usher an ascended age of existence. The faction draws unprincipled transmuters, fringe scientists, and irrational astronomers to its academy and observatory, the Cosmic Oculus, where they receive fractured instructions from the faction's five leaders, known as the Starspeakers.

These communications have a consistent message: Faction members must transmute the flora and fauna surrounding the Cosmic Oculus. Invariably, this involves transforming plants into hostile, flesh-eating specimens and mutating beasts to rearrange organs, add joints to limbs, and cause them to secrete slime. In doing so, the faction hopes to gain the attention of alien entities they believe will descend and warp all worlds in their path.

The faction members are united in purpose but not in execution. Some pursue their own theories of mutation and transfiguration, experimenting on themselves as much as on other subjects. Some instructions communicated by the Starspeakers conflict with others, as though the alien entities they seek to communicate with weren't working in concert. These contradictions mean that the faction's work advances erratically, with rejected experiments as common as transformations deemed to be in concordance with the aliens' will.

entries.name: Dawnrise Canyon
entries: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members carry out most transmutations far from public scrutiny. The faction is based in the secluded Dawnrise Canyon, far below the clifftop where the Cosmic Oculus stands. The once-tranquil canyon is now a dangerous valley of frightening creatures, hostile plants, aggressive transmuters, and wandering aberrations drawn to the unnatural landscape. Time moves erratically in the region thanks to frequent use of time-altering magic to speed up or slow down specific mutations.

entries.name: Opposition to the Far Realm
entries: While outsiders might not comprehend the distinction between the alien intelligences the Starspeakers commune with and the monsters of the Far Realm, Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members fear and reject the Far Realm as unknowable, indescribable, and inimical to life. The faction works to counter Far Realm incursions and expels any members who deal directly with that domain of incomprehensible horror.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn lacks a rigid hierarchy, but its leaders maintain careful control over the information they receive from both members' experiments and alien intelligences.

entries.name: Member Roles
entries: Certain members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn have special roles in the faction.

entries.name: Starspeakers
entries: The five enigmatic Starspeakers command the entire faction. None answer to any name besides their title, and they rarely leave the Cosmic Oculus except to measure progress within Dawnrise Canyon. Four Starspeakers (Medium {@creature Aberrant Cultist|XMM|Aberrant Cultists}) are human. The fifth and most senior Starspeaker appears to be an elderly human astronomer, but she is actually a magically disguised {@creature Aboleth|XMM} who has eschewed the Far Realm.

entries.name: Worldwarpers
entries: Most faction members work at the Cosmic Oculus or Dawnrise Canyon, but others, called Worldwarpers, venture into civilized lands to engage in more far-flung experimentation. Worldwarpers seek out willing recipients to, as they put it, "gain blessings from beyond the stars."

Worldwarpers might offer to improve a banker's garden with voracious plants to deter thieves, provide an aberration to help guard a prison, or augment a diplomat's body to produce intoxicating pheromones. Like the work in Dawnrise Canyon, these puzzling changes ostensibly further a wider agenda, but Worldwarpers are rarely aware of the end goals; they merely put pieces in place as commanded and report back to the Starspeakers.

entries.name: Blots
entries: The Starspeakers secretly assign faction members to find and eradicate Far Realm sympathizers. These individuals, known within the faction as Blots, also venture into places where the Far Realm's stain bleeds into the world, seeking to quash the Far Realm's presence wherever they find it.

entries.name: Things Beyond the Stars
entries: The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives messages from many alien intelligences, not all of which are aligned with one another. You can use the Alien Entities table to generate sample intelligences that are directing the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.
The multiverse is vast and full of entities you can't imagine. I judge not those who seek guidance from the stars—though if innocents come to harm, these experimenters will regret their choices.

entries.caption: Alien Entities
rows: Atropus, the World Born Dead, is a malevolent entity the size of a planetoid that drifts ever closer to the world.
Dendar, the Night Serpent, is a colossal beast that feeds on nightmares generated by its warped mind.
Tharizdun, the Chained God, is a dark spiral of roiling nothingness. It seeks freedom from its millennia-long imprisonment and the extinction of all life.
Xhalovix is an amalgamation of 9,999 mutated planets preparing to ascend to godhood once it has transformed its ten-thousandth world.

Trapped beneath a ruined city, Zargon the Returner seeks loyal worshippers to restore his mutation-steeped realm of slime and decadence. The dark sky reveals his malign will to those who know how to interpret it.
Ejected from the Negative Plane, a nameless evil entity drives mortals to despair by twisting reality into impossible forms.

entries.name: Joining the Bringers
entries: Transmuters might seek out the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn even if they don't wish to advance the faction's goals. Faction members are undeniable masters of Transmutation magic, and some daring characters might join long enough to learn their secrets. Although some transmuters escape the faction, far too many begin to believe the Starspeakers' ramblings and become devotees—or worse, they become unwilling subjects for experimental mutations when their disloyalty is uncovered.

entries.name: Cosmic Oculus
entries: Once an abandoned observatory, the Cosmic Oculus became the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn's base when the faction discovered that the facility seems to magically amplify the messages of entities between the stars. In addition to the Starspeakers, faction astronomers also live in the Cosmic Oculus to record psychic signals from deep space and make nightly measurements of celestial bodies.

Most faction members never see the inside of the Cosmic Oculus. The ramshackle buildings clustered along the cliff face between the observatory and the canyon have expanded and mutated on their own, and members have used spells such as {@spell Stone Shape|XPHB} and {@spell Fabricate|XPHB} to haphazardly extend walls, enclose laboratories, and create passageways through the rock.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn by engaging in aberrant transmutations or completing faction quests to recover rare ritual ingredients, samples of unusual flora and fauna, or astronomical measurements from distant locations. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Renown
rows: You can freely enter Dawnrise Canyon, though you are afforded no specific protections from its dangers.
The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn warns you when you travel near places with Far Realm influence or a significant number of Aberrations.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Scroll, Potion, or Wondrous Item category.

{@dice 1d4} {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists}, convinced you embody a prophecy, become your loyal followers. You can order this retinue to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members.
{@dice 1d4} {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} join your retinue of loyal followers.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction teaches you its transmuting magic. You always have the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members.

Faction members openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown score reaches 50, you can undertake voluntary mutations to enhance your physiology. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Characters
entries: Most members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are transmutation-focused mages, but any characters with an interest in astronomy, aberrations, or warping life are welcome. New recruits aren't permitted to balk at the faction's creations or goals.

The most welcome recruits are {@class Sorcerer|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Sorcerer|XPHB|Aberrant Sorcery|Aberrant|XPHB} subclass), {@class Warlock|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Warlock|XPHB|Great Old One Patron|Great Old One|XPHB} subclass), or {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Transmuter|Transmuter|AU} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, or {@skill Nature|XPHB} or with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} are also valued as recruits, as are characters with the {@background Cosmic Dawn Experiment|AU}, {@background Guide|XPHB}, or {@background Hermit|XPHB} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Starwatcher Gear
entries: The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn provide you with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} and a blank notebook in which to record your astronomical observations.

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinket|AU|Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can easily serve as a villainous or amoral organization in your campaign. If the characters pursue villains to the Celestial Oculus, you can determine whether the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn fight the characters with the aid of powerful Transmutation magic and strange Aberrations, or if they turn out to be curious intellectuals duped by malign influences.

However, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn need not be villains. The characters might need the faction's extensive knowledge of Transmutation magic to undo a shape-shifting curse or restore a transmuted ally to the proper form. Members' whispers about creatures from the depths of space might presage an incursion by conquering githyanki astride dragons or a fleet of mind flayers on spelljamming vessels.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Covenant of the Grave
entries: The Covenant of the Grave is a loose affiliation of necromancers and those interested in studying death and undeath through a disciplined, scientific lens. The covenant has no room for megalomaniacs who seek domination via hordes of undead minions.

These realists are aware that their studies, no matter how clinical, unnerve most people, so their members are unobtrusive and their laboratories hidden. The greatest covenant academy is the Pale Tower, a morbid, bone-white structure far from civilization.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Covenant members are typically more interested in deepening their knowledge than their power. They freely share their research with each other via correspondence, personal visits, or clandestine lectures, but they rarely reveal discoveries to those outside the organization. Many worry that their research might be misused for sinister, nonacademic ends. Others simply don't expect anyone but like-minded scholars to comprehend their work.

Unlike necromancers who incite undead uprisings, the Covenant of the Grave usually works to stymie undead hordes and return less powerful undead to the safer confines of the laboratory or grave. Members consider undead rampages dreadfully unscientific, if not outright embarrassing. They're keenly aware of the harm that such villainous necromancy brings to the faction's reputation. Their opposition to necromantic wickedness sometimes puts the faction in conflict with powerful undead such as liches, death knights, or vampires.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: Although an established hierarchy exists within the Covenant of the Grave, members are usually too engrossed in their own research to worry about rank.

entries.name: Necrodemics and Gravetenders
entries: Any faction member who shares a significant scholarly truth about death, decay, or undeath with the faction might gain the title of Necrodemic. Some members hold expanded titles such as Arisen Necrodemic or Necrodemic Embalmist, awarded for sharing more complex knowledge.

The title of Gravetender is held by the three head administrators of the Pale Tower. Emeritus administrators keep this title after retirement, so four to six Gravetenders usually exist at a time. Gravetenders set the overall direction for the faction but are usually bookish and circumspect, so change within the faction is gradual.

entries.name: Joining the Covenant

entries.title: Members of the Covenant of the Grave show respect to undead individuals who allow themselves to be studied.

entries: Any spellcaster with an interest in Necromancy magic or macabre research is likely to hear about the Covenant of the Grave, but the faction doesn't actively recruit. The covenant expects aspirants to independently identify its members and present a well-reasoned proposal for membership. A member who receives a qualified aspirant usually confers with other members before either taking on the aspirant as a research assistant or sending them to study at the Pale Tower.

entries.name: Undead Members
entries: Only a few members of the Covenant of the Grave are undead. Covenant members have little use for less powerful undead such as skeletons and zombies, and other undead are usually too consumed by their hungers to maintain the intellectual rigor the covenant expects. The Undead Members table details the few undead scholars in the covenant.

entries.caption: Undead Members
rows: A bookish {@creature Ghost|XMM} who haunts his surgical theater, Adlin is so tied to his experiments that he's unaware he's dead.
The Lawful Neutral {@creature Lich|XMM} Kadra hides that she's undead so her highly regarded insights into lichdom seem inspired by intellect rather than a study of her own nature.
A determined {@creature Revenant|XMM}, Melodin is a Gravetender of the Pale Tower who seeks to avenge herself against her predecessor by proving herself the superior administrator.

entries.name: The Pale Tower
entries: The greatest concentration of covenant members resides in the Pale Tower. Rising from a noxious swamp, this bone-white structure is thousands of years old. The tower's small, dingy exterior belies its underground warren of classrooms, laboratories, and ossuaries.

In addition to being an academy and research institution, the Pale Tower is a repository of sinister necromantic magic that the covenant doesn't want misused. Rumors hold that malicious artifacts, lost Necromancy spells, and soul-staining magic items are locked away in vaults only the Gravetenders can access.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Covenant of the Grave by sharing scholarly insights into death or undeath or by completing quests for the Covenant. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Covenant of the Grave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Covenant of the Grave Renown
rows: You receive free lodging at the Pale Tower and can access its extensive subterranean libraries. The covenant safely contains or destroys malevolent magic items you surrender to its care.
You can purchase the costly Material components required for Necromancy spells you can cast from covenant members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the covenant gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Rod or Wand category.
Covenant members freely cast the {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell on you and your allies.

You earn the honorary title of Necrodemic. When you surrender a magic item to the covenant, the covenant gifts you a different magic item of an equal or lesser rarity from the same category as the surrendered item.
You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Gravetenders. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction shares necromantic secrets with you. You always have the {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

You earn the honorary title of Arisen Necrodemic. You can request the help of {@dice 1d4} {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages} for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

If you or one of your allies dies and the body is brought to the Pale Tower, a covenant member casts a {@spell Resurrection|XPHB} spell, targeting the deceased. This reward is free the first time you use it. On subsequent occasions, you must provide any Material components normally consumed by the spell.

entries.name: Covenant of the Grave Characters
entries: Joining the Covenant of the Grave is advantageous to any character interested in the secrets of life and death. While intellectual rigor is important, knowledge of any death-adjacent subject is sufficient for aspiring members.

The most welcome aspirants are {@class Cleric|XPHB}, {@class Monk|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Necromancer|Necromancer|AU} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, or {@skill Medicine|XPHB}; proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB}; or the {@background Covenant of the Grave Recruit|AU}, {@background Sage|XPHB}, or {@background Scribe|XPHB} background are also good fits.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Covenant of the Grave, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Grave Services
entries: The covenant respectfully performs final rites for your corpse whenever the inevitable comes to pass.

entries.name: Modest Lifestyle
entries: The covenant pays you a stipend that supports your {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle (1 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Covenant of the Grave Trinket|AU|Covenant of the Grave Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the covenant.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: Faction members might warn the characters of potential necromantic uprisings or escort the party through lands plagued with undead. Having access to graveyards and burial houses, the faction might also recover the corpse of someone the characters want to revive or question.

The covenant isn't likely to aid the characters for free. Members might request lost necromantic lore in exchange for their help or task the party with defeating a necromancer or undead creature who has rejected the covenant's academic overtures.

entries.title: Two necromancers cast the {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB} spell on a nearby corpse in a graveyard.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Covenant of the Grave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Crucible Keepers
entries: The Crucible Keepers consists of daredevil evokers who venture into natural or magical disasters to study the phenomenal power at play. Some members use their Evocation magic to counter disasters and help others, while other members revel in nature's destructive forces and take inspiration from them to enhance their own devastating spellcraft.

entries.name: Goals and Activities

entries.title: Crucible Keepers love a good explosion.

entries: Crucible Keepers study Evocation magic to command energy and control powerful forces. They eschew solitary scholarship, preferring informal gatherings where they exchange ideas and try to impress their peers with spectacular displays of magical might.

Faction members might be thrill seekers, but they aren't fools. They plan their dangerous endeavors well in advance, spending days or weeks charting natural or magical phenomena before enjoying the rush of soaring through the eye of a hurricane or surfing a lava flow. They employ protective magic while engaging in these endeavors, and they're quick to chide fools who confront danger unprepared.
Overuse of powerful evocation magic can warp the land as well as the souls of those who become drunk on magical power. The Crucible Keepers' attempt to right these wrongs is noble.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: Those drawn to the Crucible Keepers aren't the sort who like following orders.
