Ranks within the Crucible Keepers are unofficial, fluid, and based on frequent competitive challenges between members, with losers acknowledging winners' higher rank. Challenges usually involve magical duels, elaborate races, or dangerous stunts.

entries.name: Joining the Crucible Keepers
entries: The Crucible Keepers enthusiastically welcomes anyone who wants to try out for its ranks. Gaining membership is as simple as impressing any faction member with a clever display of Evocation magic, a wild physical stunt, or a dramatic parlor trick.

entries.name: Eljar Charscale
entries: The current head of the Crucible Keepers is a dragonborn named Eljar Charscale (Medium {@creature Evoker Archmage|AU}; see {@book chapter 6|AU|6}). Originally a human, Eljar was executed by cruel generals when he refused to use his magic in an unpopular war. After his allies reincarnated him, Eljar fled in his new dragonborn body. He took the name Charscale on joining the Crucible Keepers.

Eljar loves the thrill of Evocation magic and is undefeated in duels of spellcraft. In addition to his magical talent, Eljar is respected for listening to everyone and offering sensible guidance. He began leading the Crucible Keepers only a few months ago after the former leader died in a forest fire.

Eljar has a strong antiwar stance that he disseminates throughout the organization. He has forbidden members of the Crucible Keepers from serving as military battle mages. Some evokers believe this stance restricts their career paths, but most understand the reasoning behind Eljar's policy.

entries.name: Disaster Chasers
entries: Crucible Keepers predict and study natural and magical disasters, both to warn those who will be affected and to explore nature's incredible power. You can roll on or choose a result from the Pending Disasters table to generate a sample disaster Crucible Keepers plan to address.

entries.caption: Pending Disasters
rows: An undersea volcano near a busy bay is showing signs of an imminent eruption. Crucible Keepers who can operate underwater rush to study it and warn those nearby of its dangers.
Oracles predict a terrible earthquake will devastate a metropolis in the next few weeks. Crucible Keepers race to construct magical pylons to absorb its earth-rending energy.

A gate to the Elemental Plane of Fire is expected to appear in remote farmland. Crucible Keepers hope to stabilize and eventually close the gate—but before closing it, they want to venture through it to study planar conflagrations.

An ancient white dragon that planned to bury a peaceful valley beneath an avalanche has been slain. Crucible Keepers study the weakened snowpack so they can redirect the avalanche away from the nearby villages.

entries.name: Caldera Arcadium
entries: Although members believe that nature is the best classroom, the Crucible Keepers maintains a learning institution focused on Evocation magic. The Caldera Arcadium is a large stone building hanging over the rim of an active volcano, suspended by enormous metal chains and struts.

The temperature inside the building ranges from unpleasantly warm to blisteringly hot, but eager students fill its three classrooms every day. The building also holds magical forges for the study and creation of magic items. A stone bridge from the Arcadium's roof leads to dormitories, academic offices, and a cafeteria, all hanging off the volcano's edge.

The Caldera Arcadium's headmaster is a scholarly {@creature Efreeti|XMM} named Nadia Flameheart, who taught magic in the City of Brass for a millennium before joining the Crucible Keepers. The only wishes she entertains are those for better grades, and her only responses are tips for studying.

Fire-blackened {@creature Stone Golem|XMM|Stone Golems} called the Scorchborn provide security for the Arcadium, a duty that mostly involves defusing fights between hotheaded students. The Scorchborn are also instrumental to the wards that protect the school from volcanic eruptions, but not even Nadia Flameheart understands how. Since all Scorchborn are identical, no one is sure how many there are. No danger has yet presented a sufficient threat to marshal them all in one place.

Arcadium students frequently engage in death-defying stunts they call "field trips." The most common stunt is a leap from an Arcadium balcony during an eruption, trusting an ordinary rope to prevent a fall into lava. Another popular field trip involves launching homemade hang gliders from the volcano's edge.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Crucible Keepers by surviving natural disasters or by completing Crucible Keeper missions. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Crucible Keepers Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Crucible Keepers Renown
rows: The Crucible Keepers sends you advance notice of natural disasters in your area.
The Crucible Keepers permits you and your companions to stay at the Caldera Arcadium.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Crucible Keepers gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Wand or Weapon category.
You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Evocation spells while at the Caldera Arcadium.

A reckless {@creature Mage Apprentice|XMM} becomes your loyal fan. You can order this apprentice to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
Eljar Charscale or Nadia Flameheart meets with you at your request. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the Crucible Keepers teaches you magic to guard you from the elements. You always have the {@spell Daylight|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Faction members openly share information with you. You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Evocation spells while at the Caldera Arcadium.

You can call for an {@creature Efreeti|XMM} to aid you with a single task; the DM determines whether the efreeti can grant a {@spell Wish|XPHB}. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

entries.name: Crucible Keepers Characters
entries: The Crucible Keepers welcomes anyone willing to study destruction up close, which brings a high proportion of daredevils and thrill seekers into its ranks. Characters who are {@class Barbarian|XPHB}, {@class Druid|XPHB}, {@class Sorcerer|XPHB}, or {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Evoker|Evoker|XPHB} subclass) are likely to be sought after as members, as are those with proficiency in {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} or with the {@background Crucible Storm Chaser|AU} or {@background Noble|XPHB} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Crucible Keepers, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Poor Lifestyle
entries: The Crucible Keepers pays you a stipend that supports a {@book Poor|XPHB|6|Poor (2 SP per Day)} lifestyle (2 SP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Crucible Keepers Trinket|AU|Crucible Keepers Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time in the Crucible Keepers.

entries.name: Using This Faction

entries.title: Members of the Crucible Keepers face each other in magical combat. It's harmless and all in good fun.

entries: Crucible Keepers are often harbingers of catastrophe. If they appear in large numbers, it's usually because they anticipate an imminent disaster. A Crucible Keeper traveling through a dangerous area might hire the party to escort them, but it would be wise to ask what awaits at the journey's end.

However, Crucible Keepers are evokers, not diviners, so their guesses are sometimes wrong. As the DM, you can decide whether that means the disaster doesn't happen, is earlier or later by days, or is some other event entirely.

Crucible Keepers also study the aftermath of disasters, both natural and magical. Their presence might be a detriment or a blessing for recovery efforts. Unscrupulous members revel in disasters' aftermath and might seek to profit from them, while selfless members work to ease suffering.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Crucible Keepers can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Horizon Weavers
entries: The Horizon Weavers is a collection of far-flung conjurers, explorers, and scholars who practice summoning, teleportation, and planar travel.

Members of the Horizon Weavers have unparalleled wanderlust; they've seen sights and lived through experiences most would consider too wild to be true. However, the faction's planar sojourns have not gone unnoticed, and members now work to avert the attention of a malevolent extraplanar entity fixated on their organization.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Horizon Weavers hone their expertise in all forms of Conjuration magic, from summoning to creation to teleportation, with a focus on extraplanar travel. Powerful Horizon Weavers create gates between planes, while junior members catalog known gates or simply wander through to see what's on the other side. New faction members usually begin by traveling their own world to experience different climates and cultures before exploring other planes.

Many faction members are also amateur or professional artisans; some weave textiles as well as magic. Horizon Weavers often incorporate spells such as {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} or {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} into their everyday lives, using magic for everything from companionship to household chores.

entries.name: Horizon Weaver Cloaks
entries: Each new member who joins the faction receives a durable cloak with their initials sewn into the collar. Horizon Weavers recognize these garments on sight and seek to retrieve any that are lost or stolen.

A Horizon Weaver's cloak repels water and protects its wearer from most types of weather. The faction replaces damaged cloaks when necessary. Some members weave the threads of former cloaks into new ones.

Many Horizon Weavers incorporate their cloaks into magic items they create. The most popular choices are {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG}, {@item Cloak of Protection|XDMG}, and {@item Clothes of Mending|XDMG}.

entries.name: The Lurker
entries: A massive beast from the liminal space between planes menaces the Horizon Weavers. This entity, known as the Lurker, towers higher than mountains, with immense pincers and a single, enormous eye that radiates malice and reflects strange lights and lines.

Several months ago, when faction members first glimpsed the Lurker, a powerful team of Horizon Weavers set out to confront the monster. The team went missing, and the Lurker has since become more aggressive, snapping at some Horizon Weavers in the split second it takes them to magically travel between planes. Sometimes this shears the unlucky traveler in half; other times, the individual never reappears. These incidents are rare, but all Horizon Weavers worry about a potential Lurker strike with each planar trip.
Those who provide shelter and aid to explorers of this vast multiverse are friends to both me and Mystra.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: As befits members of a society of explorers, Horizon Weavers are widely scattered. A wandering Horizon Weaver might go weeks or months without seeing another member, and a meeting might be coincidental. Senior faction members, called Gatemakers, settle disputes or provide advice, although reaching a Gatemaker often requires a cross-planar trek.

entries.title: When necessary, members of the Horizon Weavers call on powerful allies from other planes of existence.

entries.name: Way Stations and Shuttles
entries: Not all Horizon Weavers seek endless travel. Some stay in one place for months or years, perhaps with a friend or lover they met during their travels. Horizon Weavers who remain in one place are expected to maintain way stations, providing directions, supplies, and shelter to passing faction members.

Weaving slang is common in these way stations: a "shuttle" is a traveler, a "beam" is a well-established way station, a "weft" is a member with irrepressible wanderlust, and a "heddle" is someone reliable.
You can roll on the Planar Way Stations table to generate a sample way station or odd planar locale.

entries.caption: Planar Way Stations
rows: A gnome named Molly Nettle (Small {@creature Conjurer Archmage|AU}) keeps a gingerbread house in the {@book Feywild|XDMG|5|Feywild} where she welcomes Horizon Weavers but shoos away all others. She doesn't understand why visitors find her residence and her child-shaped cookie sculptures off-putting.

The Tidepool Larder is an air-filled grotto on the Elemental Plane of Water, stocked with salted fish and other seafood. The reclusive {@creature Marid|XMM} caretaker, Baliob, hides from visitors and doesn't charge for supplies.
A dour {@creature Githzerai Psion|XMM} named Ut maintains a peaceful monastery called Ninebells on a rocky island in Limbo. Ut lets non-Horizon Weavers stay no more than nine hours.

Scuttlebeam is a beached ship in a Feywild forest. Its married keepers, a goliath named Rusty Jenk (Medium {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}) and an orc named Trellie (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM}), don't remember how the ship got here.
Falling Up, a floating inn in the Elemental Plane of Air, is managed by three human, semiretired Horizon Weavers (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages}), all eager to swap tales.
A way station in Bytopia called the Shuttle's Rest was recently reduced to ruins by an enormous, clawed creature.

entries.name: Joining the Horizon Weavers
entries: Any curious adventurer who longs to explore the unknown might join the faction after meeting a Horizon Weaver. An extended conversation with a member is all it takes to earn a second meeting, when the member presents the aspirant with a Horizon Weaver cloak and officially inducts them into the organization. An inducting member without weaving skills or connections might invite the new member to create their own Horizon Weaver cloak, though it must be made to the faction's specifications.

entries.name: Spiral Conservatory
entries: Deep in a forest on the Material Plane stands a twisting building of wood and stone that surrounds a grassy courtyard. This is the Spiral Conservatory, the first and largest Horizon Weaver way station. Here, students of Conjuration magic and planar lore learn to navigate hazardous environments, summon helpful creatures, and conjure useful equipment.

The Spiral Conservatory is located at a confluence of ley lines that provides numerous, if inconstant, gates to Arcadia, the Beastlands, and the Feywild. Fey and intelligent animals often wander through the Spiral Conservatory; some of them delight in mentoring eager Horizon Weavers.

A tiefling named Gallinaver the Heddle (Medium {@creature Conjurer Archmage|AU}; {@book chapter 6|AU|6|Archmages}) serves as the Spiral Conservatory's chief caretaker. Gallinaver and his husband, a soft-spoken {@creature Djinni|XMM} named Cloud Lace, are the easiest Gatemakers to contact, as they're never far from the Spiral Conservatory.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Horizon Weavers by displaying planar knowledge, conjuring magical wonders, reporting previously unknown planar gates, or completing excursions for the faction. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Horizon Weavers Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Horizon Weavers Renown
rows: You can consult with the Horizon Weavers to receive general information about a plane you intend to visit.
You can stay in any way station maintained by a Horizon Weaver (including the Spiral Conservatory).

The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the faction gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Armor or Wondrous Item category. Alternatively, if you're a member, the faction can craft your faction cloak into an Uncommon magic item of your choice.
You receive a 10 percent discount when buying armor, weapons, and adventuring gear from a Horizon Weaver way station.

You are given one of a pair of {@item Sending Stones|XDMG}; the other is held by a mid-level faction member. If you are lost in an extraplanar location the faction can reach, you can use the Sending Stone to call the faction for help. {@dice 1d4} {@creature Scout Captain|XMM|Scout Captains} then arrive to escort you to a safe destination. If your Renown Score drops below 20, your Sending Stone is confiscated.
The discount you receive at way stations increases to 20 percent.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction teaches you to traverse liminal spaces. You always have the {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Gatemakers. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

Faction members can cast the {@spell Plane Shift|XPHB} spell at your behest, transporting you and your allies to an extraplanar location of your choice. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

entries.name: Horizon Weavers Characters
entries: The Horizon Weavers welcome carefree, capable wanderers who yearn to see what's over the horizon or through a planar portal.

{@class Druid|XPHB}, {@class Ranger|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Conjurer|Conjurer|AU} subclass) are excellent fits. Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}; proficiency with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB}; or the {@background Artisan|XPHB}, {@background Guide|XPHB}, {@background Horizon Weaver Initiate|AU}, or {@background Wayfarer|XPHB} background are also welcome.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Horizon Weavers, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Traveling Cloak
entries: You receive a distinctive Horizon Weavers cloak and a set of {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Horizon Weavers Trinket|AU|Horizon Weavers Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Horizon Weavers.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Horizon Weavers might give out quests, such as mapmaking or rescue missions, that require travel to distant places. They might also seek the adventurers' help dealing with the threat of the {@area Lurker|216|x}.

The Horizon Weavers can also rescue characters stranded in distant or inhospitable places, such as those sent to other planes by the {@spell Prismatic Spray|XPHB} or {@spell Prismatic Wall|XPHB} spell. Lost characters might be lucky enough to find a Horizon Weaver way station.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Horizon Weavers can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Ninth Quill

entries.title: Members of the Ninth Quill plot the heist of magical lore.

entries: The Ninth Quill is a faction of thieves, saboteurs, and spies who use magic to obtain and sequester powerful artifacts and knowledge by any means necessary—including robbing and sabotaging other factions. The faction's leaders consider their organization to be superior to factions focused on a specific school of magic and the safest custodian of dangerous lore and relics, but some members also steal valuables and undermine other organizations for personal gain.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Ninth Quill members' adaptability and diverse areas of expertise help them infiltrate other groups, often posing as new recruits or long-absent members from other lands.
The Ninth Quill has a few popular catchphrases that members use as meaningful mantras—or excuses for criminality. These phrases are described in the sections that follow.

entries.name: Our Hands Are Safest
entries: Ninth Quill members often steal magic items and research to keep them out of others' hands. They receive extensive training in handling dangerous artifacts and resisting the influence of sentient objects. In principle, these items are sequestered in the Ninth Quill vaults (which members insist are more secure than any other faction's), but less scrupulous members might keep certain items for their own use.

entries.name: Others Learn So We Can Earn
entries: When the Ninth Quill steals discoveries and relics that aren't particularly harmful, it sells them to wealthy patrons to fund its operations. Desperate buyers rebuffed by other factions, such as a necromancer rejected by the {@area Covenant of the Grave|1ed|x} or a transmuter suspicious of the {@area Bringers of Cosmic Dawn|1d8|x}, might seek the services of the Ninth Quill to obtain such objects.

entries.name: Discontent Is Our Best Defense
entries: The Ninth Quill seeks to destabilize other factions that become too powerful. This often involves agents infiltrating a faction, then undertaking whisper campaigns, sabotaging experiments, and encouraging critical personnel to depart. The Ninth Quill agents quietly slip away once they have stoked sufficient inefficiency, paranoia, and infighting.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The Ninth Quill values intelligence, resourcefulness, and loyalty. A significant majority of Ninth Quill agents use spellcasting to enhance their spy craft.

entries.name: A Careful Hierarchy
entries: Although Ninth Quill leaders take pains to hide their identities, the faction operates under a strict hierarchal system. Agents are the lowest ranking, followed by Lieutenants, followed by Masters. Those in the highest echelon are Guild Masters.

entries.name: Joining the Ninth Quill
entries: The Ninth Quill operates in the shadows and therefore doesn't entertain applicants. However, the Guild Masters keep an eye on talented thieves and other morally ambiguous individuals with magical skills. If the Guild Masters believe such an individual would be an asset to the Ninth Quill, they extend an invitation to visit Blackscript College—through an anonymous courier, of course.

entries.name: Blackscript College
entries: The hidden academy where the Ninth Quill trains its members is located in a crime-ridden neighborhood of a busy trade city. Dilapidated warehouses, all owned by the Ninth Quill, surround the college to ensure its privacy. There's no readily apparent entrance; instead, it's accessible only by unmarked doors in twisting alleys and hidden passages.

The centuries-old college was once a legitimate magical academy, but city records show that it closed decades ago due to administrative corruption. In truth, the college simply went underground to teach magical spy craft and thievery.

A former instructor at Blackscript College's predecessor academy, the college's dean is the elf Sirethe Slipshadow (Medium {@creature Spy Master|XMM}). Slipshadow is infamous for her ability to impersonate others and uses these skills to observe students during their studies and on early missions.

The college's library, called the Repository, holds an eclectic variety of stolen treasures. An adjacent chamber called the Ersatz Repository contains worktables where members make high-quality counterfeits of spellbooks, relics, and artifacts. Many cherished treasures held by other factions are actually Ninth Quill counterfeits.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Ninth Quill by completing Ninth Quill missions or by contributing stolen magical lore or magic items. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Ninth Quill Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Ninth Quill Renown
rows: You and your companions receive free lodging at Ninth Quill safe houses, which are present in many cities.
You can buy Common potions and Spell Scrolls from Ninth Quill members.

If the authorities are searching for you, the Ninth Quill dispatches numerous faction members who are magically disguised to look like you. This might allow you to evade capture for days or months, at the DM's discretion. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 15, the Ninth Quill gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Repository.
You receive a magical decoder that allows you to read written Thieves' Cant. If your Renown Score drops below 20, this decoder is confiscated.

The Ninth Quill can provide you with a believable but useless duplicate of a magic item you show them. Creating the duplicate takes {@dice 1d4} days of work. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, Ninth Quill faction members teach you how to magically shroud yourself. You always have the {@spell Nondetection|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can buy Uncommon and Rare potions and Spell Scrolls from Ninth Quill members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Ninth Quill gives you a Very Rare magic item that another faction desperately wants to recover.

entries.name: Ninth Quill Characters
entries: The Ninth Quill uses thieves and enforcers, but the group is no mere criminal guild; its leaders prefer recruits who have magical skill or knowledge.

The most welcome are {@class Bard|XPHB}, {@class Fighter|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Fighter|XPHB|Eldritch Knight|Eldritch Knight|XPHB} subclass), {@class Rogue|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Rogue|XPHB|Arcane Trickster|Arcane Trickster|XPHB} subclass), {@class Warlock|XPHB}, or {@class Wizard|XPHB}. Characters with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Deception|XPHB}; the {@background Agent of the Ninth Quill|AU}, {@background Charlatan|XPHB}, or {@background Criminal|XPHB} background; or the {@feat Magic Initiate|XPHB} feat are also valued.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Ninth Quill, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Modest Lifestyle
entries: The Ninth Quill pays you a stipend to support your {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle (1 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Ninth Quill Trinket|AU|Ninth Quill Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Ninth Quill.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Ninth Quill often opposes other magical factions. You might introduce Ninth Quill {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} or {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} looking to steal the characters' hard-won items or lore, or you could establish intrigue-laden plots about Ninth Quill {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies}, {@creature Spy Master|XMM|Spy Masters}, or {@creature Bandit Deceiver|XMM|Bandit Deceivers} who stoke rivalries and paranoia within another faction.

Alternatively, the Ninth Quill could employ or aid the characters. The faction might recruit the characters to retrieve a valuable asset or assist them with recovering and disposing of a dangerous artifact. You could even build a campaign around efforts to steal relics from each of the other magical factions.
Good intentions are commonplace among members of the Ninth Quill, but never drop your guard around them.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Ninth Quill can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Phantasmic Circus

entries.title: Members of the Phantasmic Circus prepare for a magic-enhanced performance.

entries: Part entertainers' alliance and part traveling carnival, the Phantasmic Circus is an organization of performers and illusionists who create grand spectacles and share magical techniques to delight, entertain, and misdirect.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: The Phantasmic Circus stages elaborate performances across the world, moving from city to city to bring delight and wonder. These performances are huge extravaganzas involving dozens of entertainers and drawing large audiences. The circus is renowned for illusions and pyrotechnics that reach hundreds of feet into the air.

These complex routines change with every show; Phantasmic Circus performers are always experimenting with new illusions, death-defying stunts, and musical accompaniment. Tickets and concessions are pricey, but audience members remember the faction's thrilling spectacles for the rest of their lives.

The Phantasmic Circus's performances use trained creatures for certain acts, but audience members would be shocked to realize how few genuine creatures are on display. Lifelike illusions of animals and monsters perform most stunts, while living animals are treated carefully and kept out of danger.

entries.name: One Circus, Many Troupes
entries: The Phantasmic Circus isn't a single traveling troupe, but rather the collective name for several groups that operate independently, each under the guidance of a manager called a Wondermaker. Circus members might shift from group to group to hone their skills, so residents of a city might never realize that the "Phantasmic Circus" that visited twice the previous year was actually two different troupes.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The astounding and popular Phantasmic Circus of today had humble beginnings as a small traveling carnival called the Hayver and Hayver Circus. When the Hayvers' youngest sibling, the human Della, returned to the family circus with training in Illusion magic and a gregarious gnome husband named Walnip Waddlebell, the circus started its meteoric rise.

Soon, Della and Walnip were running the circus as its ringmasters and self-appointed "First Maestros." The couple also gave the increasingly illusion-focused show a flashier name. The other Hayvers have since passed away, but the aging First Maestros (both Small {@creature Performer Legend|XMM|Performer Legends}), still plan spectacles, train new illusionists, and orchestrate the many troupes operating as the Phantasmic Circus.

entries.name: Wondermakers
entries: The First Maestros are now too old to tour, but they keep in touch with each troupe as its travels bring it back to the circus's headquarters, the Mirage Lyceum. The First Maestros appoint a Wondermaker to guide each troupe. Most Wondermakers are flashy showoffs or grand illusionists who enjoy the spotlight as ringmasters or star performers. In other troupes, the Wondermaker works behind the scenes, guiding the performers and pushing their shows to new heights.

Each Wondermaker keeps their troupe's books, protects its members, makes its travel plans, and coordinates with other Wondermakers to ensure they aren't revisiting cities too soon. They also send performers from troupe to troupe to teach gifted members additional skills or to resolve personality clashes.

entries.name: Roustabouts
entries: Although acrobats, illusionists, animals, and entertainers are the stars of the Phantasmic Circus, a platoon of supporters keeps the troupe running. Collectively called roustabouts, these laborers and guides let the performers take the glory while collecting reasonable pay from the troupe's Wondermaker. The visual artists who design the elaborate sets and costumes are also roustabouts; they mentor each other to hone their artistic skills.
Mystra smiles on those who pluck the Weave to provide entertainment to the public. So do I—as long as that entertainment cloaks no foul deeds.

entries.name: Circus Acts
entries: No two Phantasmic Circus performances are the same. Roll on the Phantasmic Circus Acts table to generate a sample act as a basis for other wondrous spectacles.

entries.caption: Phantasmic Circus Acts
rows: Several Gladiators fight a beholder, which is an illusion—a hidden {@creature Performer Legend|XMM} uses the {@spell Major Image|XPHB} spell to simulate the monster.
Six trained mammoths form a pyramid, and a giant toad hops up to the top; all the animals are realistic illusions.
A {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM} sings an eerie ballad about a shipwreck while {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers} on trapezes swing over and through the illusion of a grand, doomed galley.
Two {@creature Satyr|XMM|Satyrs} play a compelling melody while they lead volunteers from the audience through a cage of glaring lions; the volunteers and lions are illusions.
Two {@creature Knight|XMM|Knights} joust while riding horses cloaked in illusions to look like rhinoceroses.
A {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM} navigates a wondrous illusory forest and grows 50 feet tall to step over the tallest tree at the act's conclusion.

entries.name: Joining the Phantasmic Circus
entries: Joining the Phantasmic Circus as a performer requires rigorous tryouts under the watchful eye of a troupe's Wondermaker, who makes final decisions about applicants. Those who wish to join the circus as roustabouts, however, need only express interest and demonstrate a relevant skill to a Wondermaker, who is usually happy to accept the additional help.

entries.name: Mirage Lyceum
entries: The headquarters of the Phantasmic Circus, the Mirage Lyceum, was formerly the winter home of the Hayver and Hayver Circus. Once a sad collection of animal pens and bunk rooms, it is now a vibrant jumble of playhouses, amphitheaters, classrooms, and studios.

The Mirage Lyceum puts on informal performances year-round. Some performers simply want to show their skills to the First Maestros; others are junior members who aren't yet ready to take to the road. This mingling of eager pupils and wise mentors makes the Mirage Lyceum an excellent place for any illusionist to learn.

Audiences come from miles around to view these informal performances, which are cheaper than the big-city spectacles. Some wonder-struck visitors stay for long periods, and a few become inspired to join the circus life.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Phantasmic Circus by contributing illusory spectacles or by completing missions for the circus. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Phantasmic Circus Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Phantasmic Circus Renown
rows: You can travel with the Phantasmic Circus, receiving food and cramped lodging (a {@book Poor|XPHB|6|Poor (2 SP per Day)} lifestyle) while you do. You can attend performances for free.
After a performance, faction members freely share with you {@dice 1d6} rumors heard from the audience members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Phantasmic Circus gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Wand or Wondrous Item category.

A troupe of {@dice 1d3 + 1} {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers} become your loyal followers. The troupe performs simple tasks, such as restocking supplies or gathering information, but they won't willingly put themselves in danger.
You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Illusion spells from faction members.

Your troupe gains an additional {@dice 1d4} {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers}. Additionally, you can ask your troupe to help you with one dangerous mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, circus members share their illusory tricks with you. You always have the {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Wondermakers or, when at the Mirage Lyceum, with the First Maestros. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
{@dice 1d4} {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM|Performer Maestros} and an additional {@dice 1d6} {@creature Performer|XMM|Performers} join your troupe.

entries.name: Phantasmic Circus Characters
entries: The Phantasmic Circus welcomes artists, entertainers, and illusionists of all types as performers, provided they impress a Wondermaker. Roustabouts can be of any class or background.

{@class Bard|XPHB}, {@class Rogue|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Illusionist|Illusionist|XPHB} subclass) are excellent fits, as are characters with proficiency in {@skill Performance|XPHB} or with the {@background Charlatan|XPHB}, {@background Entertainer|XPHB}, {@background Phantasmic Circus Trouper|AU}, or {@background Wayfarer|XPHB} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Phantasmic Circus, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Patron Connections
entries: You can always find work as an entertainer while in a settlement.

entries.name: Poor Lifestyle
entries: The circus provides you with performance proceeds to support your Poor lifestyle (2 SP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Phantasmic Circus Trinket|AU|Phantasmic Circus Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Phantasmic Circus.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: You can use the Phantasmic Circus in your campaign to enliven an urban atmosphere. Since the Phantasmic Circus travels from city to city, the characters also might encounter the faction on the road.

The Phantasmic Circus cares more about presenting grand spectacles than following local laws. As such, the circus might create inadvertent fires or spark a panicked stampede that requires the characters' intervention. Alternatively, the circus might agree to conceal fugitives who don't seem harmful, possibly enabling the party to escape a settlement without alerting the authorities.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Phantasmic Circus can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Seers of Sea and Sky
entries: The Seers of Sea and Sky is a faction of oracles who make predictions about the future based on movements of the clouds and waves. Open to all methods of divination, the seers encourage communication with a wide array of aerial and undersea prophets and meticulously record their prognostications.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: The Seers of Sea and Sky maintains libraries and reading rooms in many large, coastal cities. Within these hubs, seers cast Divination spells for reasonable costs; train other members in divination techniques; and maintain contact with visionaries across, above, and below the seas. Although obtaining accurate information through divination is important to the faction, sharing knowledge and imparting guidance to those most in need of it is also a crucial part of the faction's mission.

The seers primarily practice what they call hydromancy, or predictions based on watching the movement of water, and aeromancy, or predictions based on observing the weather. Members hone many subspecialties within these techniques. For example, some seers divine by scrutinizing driftwood delivered by ocean waves, while others base predictions on the movement of clouds.

entries.name: Allies of Air and Water
entries: Faction members live in diverse locales and include a wide array of folk. The faction's membership includes aarakocra, giant eagles, and other flying creatures who can provide detailed data about the wind and cloud movement. Other seers live beneath the waves, including bronze dragons and merfolk. Members from both groups and land-bound seers often convene, keeping the faction cohesive.

entries.name: Truth Twice
entries: The seers maintain a philosophy they call "truth twice." The faction doesn't consider a prophecy or revelation to be reliable unless it's been corroborated by another member—preferably one using a different Divination spell or method of divining. Checking and rechecking other members' work is routine. As a result, the seers' predictions have a reputation for reliability. The support members provide for each other contributes to the organization's close-knit culture.

entries.title: Members of the Seers of Sea and Sky perform powerful Divination magic outdoors to reveal terrible threats.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization
entries: The oracles who founded the Seers of Sea and Sky were called the Scholars of Deep Truth. As the scholars' fame spread and wealthy patrons sought their guidance, the scholars built an exclusive, opulent lighthouse to entertain petitioners. The scholars worked with undersea oracles to strengthen the accuracy of their own prophecies.

When several misleading prognostications left locals victims of suspicious seaside disasters, the scholars started questioning their sources. They soon discovered an {@creature Aboleth|XMM} named Naurishaul was manipulating them. Before the scholars could address this shocking news, a client exposed the scholars as minions of this malevolent undersea entity. While technically true, this announcement was misleading, as the scholars hadn't realized their answers came from such a sinister source.

entries.name: A New Beginning
entries: The scandal could have driven the scholars into hiding or ruin, but the organization publicly acknowledged its unsavory association and resolved to do better. Members established a network of mutual education and support, teaching genuine divination methods and rigorously double-checking their revelations. They kept the remote lighthouse as the faction's headquarters but established outposts to provide answers in seaside cities where petitioners of more limited means could seek guidance.

The efforts to rebuild the scholars' reputation worked. Experts in hydromancy and aeromancy joined the faction, attracted by its openness and support. Many were diviners from far-flung places, including windswept peaks and undersea communities. To reflect the organization's growing membership and shed its tainted legacy, the faction changed its name to the Seers of Sea and Sky.

Focused entirely on their divination mission, the seers eschew hierarchy. New members are expected to respect more senior members, but the faction in general has an egalitarian outlook. Beyond the Founders (see below), members consider titles and ranks unnecessary.

entries.name: The Founders
entries: The faction's inner circle consists of the original Scholars of Deep Truth members, though they use that scandal-ridden name only as a cautionary tale. Other seers simply refer to them as the Founders. With a reputation for humility, insight, and rigor, the Founders are highly regarded throughout the faction.

The Founders consist of the human siblings Kessalee Cloudseeker and Narvok Cloudseeker (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages}), haughty elf Travieste Nilvinarian (Medium {@creature Noble Prodigy|XMM}), and gregarious gnome Bulrug Seawhistle (Small {@creature Performer Maestro|XMM}). The Founders frequently travel to consult with faction members scattered across land, sea, and air environments.

entries.name: Wavewatchers
entries: Some Seers of Sea and Sky have formed a coterie called the Wavewatchers. These members enjoy watching ocean waves crash against the shore, and they spend hours in contemplation, watching light play on the waves and listening to their soothing sounds. The Wavewatchers have created a meditation trend that attracts more faction members each week. A few of the newest faction members aren't diviners at all—they're mystics or monks who've joined to seek peace from the rolling waves.

However, some faction members have fallen behind in their work in favor of wave watching, and they're producing unconfirmed divinations. This is unacceptable to the Founders, who are displeased with the Wavewatchers phenomenon. Kessalee worries that their old foe Naurishaul has infiltrated the faction once again by mesmerizing susceptible faction members.

entries.name: Remarkable Members
entries: Most members of the Seers of Sea and Sky are humanoids, but the Notable Seers table provides examples of unusual beings who have joined the faction.

entries.caption: Notable Seers
rows: Gnarlbeak, a {@creature Giant Owl|XMM}, survived a demon attack in her youth and has become an expert on predicting fiendish incursions by studying lightning storms.
The sardonic, blue-feathered {@creature Aarakocra Aeromancer|XMM} Kaekylin is eager to discuss cloud formations.
An {@creature Adult Bronze Dragon|XMM}, Quellishar can't speak and uses graceful dances to communicate truths he sees in the movements of the tides.
Tuppet, a pensive {@creature Sea Hag|XMM}, shares insights gained by watching schools of fish migrate; she's understanding if clients are cautious about interacting with a hag.
The {@creature Water Weird|XMM} Vort uses tide pools to perform scrying rituals.

entries.name: Joining the Seers of Sea and Sky
entries: Anyone with an interest in studying the sea or sky to gain insights can join the faction as a scribe or assistant for the diviners who perform the bulk of the faction's work. Joining as a diviner is more difficult. Applicants must travel to the faction's lighthouse and request membership from any senior member, who makes the final admission decision. Those who don't qualify for membership are usually still welcome to stay at the lighthouse as guests.

entries.name: Lighthouse Academy
entries: The prior incarnation of the Seers of Sea and Sky, the Scholars of Deep Truth, renovated a sprawling lighthouse as an upscale retreat for wealthy petitioners. The lighthouse remains the seers' headquarters and the Founders' home, but it has been renovated to align to the seers' new mission.
The Lighthouse Academy, as it's now known, houses dozens. New members have built outbuildings around the lighthouse and equipped them with bunk rooms, scrying chambers, and libraries.

Few residents of the Lighthouse Academy work alone; daily mentoring and mutual confirmation of predictions keep the seers in close contact with each other. Shared living spaces here outnumber individual residences.

The seers employ lighthouse keepers who know little about divination but are experts in cleaning and operating the facility. To further repair their reputation, the Founders recently had these operators construct two smaller lighthouses on nearby promontories. The new lighthouses provide additional navigational guidance to sea travelers. Many captains in turn give seers free passage, citing the value of the lighthouses while secretly believing that no seer would seek passage on a ship that wasn't destined to reach its destination safely.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Seers of Sea and Sky by delivering prophecies or completing quests. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Seers of Sea and Sky Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Seers of Sea and Sky Renown
rows: You can hire sailors and dockworkers as hirelings for half the usual cost.
You can purchase the costly Material components required for Divination spells you can cast from faction members.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the seers give you an Uncommon magic item from the Rod, Staff, or Wand category.
The seers arrange ship's passage for you on any seagoing voyage at no cost.
Allies of the seers rescue you from drowning or shipwreck, if they can reach you.

You can request the aid of {@dice 1d6} {@creature Aarakocra Skirmisher|XMM|Aarakocra Skirmishers} for one mission of your choice. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, seers share their magical insight with you. You always have the {@spell Locate Object|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You can request for one of the seers to cast the {@spell Divination|XPHB} spell for free on your behalf. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
Faction members openly share information with you. Additionally, you can arrange for an audience with the Founders. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

entries.name: Seers of Sea and Sky Characters
entries: The Seers welcome anyone interested in prophecy or who lives at the boundary between the land and the sea. Fishers, sailors, and dockworkers are no less valued than diviners and oracles.

{@class Cleric|XPHB}, {@class Druid|XPHB}, {@class Ranger|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Diviner|Diviner|XPHB} subclass) are all good fits for this faction, as are characters with proficiency in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or with the {@background Sailor|XPHB} or {@background Seer Apprentice|AU} background.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Seers of Sea and Sky, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Modest Lifestyle
entries: The seers provide you with funds to support a {@book Modest|XPHB|6|Modest (1 GP per Day)} lifestyle (1 GP per day).

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Seers of Sea and Sky Trinket|AU|Seers of Sea and Sky Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Seers of Sea and Sky.

entries.name: Seers of Sea and Sky Trinket
Using This Faction
entries: The Seers of Sea and Sky are an excellent source of prophecies to steer a campaign. Faction members receive guidance from the natural world and freely share their divinations rather than hoard them. If the natural world is somehow at risk—for example, threatened by aberrations or fiends—the seers might be the first to know.

The faction can also answer specific questions the characters might have, like where to find a necessary item. The seers are precise and careful with their divinations and therefore trustworthy—but deciphering their enigmatic guidance might lead the characters on new adventures.
All of fate is written in the Weave, and few places on the Material Plane are closer to raw magic than the sea and sky. There is wisdom is seeking truths from these places.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Seers of Sea and Sky can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

entries.name: Sheltering Hands
entries: The Sheltering Hands is a benevolent organization of abjurers and advocates who operate emergency shelters and soup kitchens in far-flung settlements. This well-respected faction uses Abjuration magic to protect the vulnerable and remove afflictions.

entries.name: Goals and Activities
entries: Sheltering Hands members are skilled abjurers who focus on providing services to the needy. Faction members solicit donations of food, money, or land, then share them in directed ways to reduce as much suffering as possible. They operate shelters, aid disease-stricken regions, and work to lift curses.

Beyond fulfilling immediate needs, members of the Sheltering Hands help individuals rebuild their dignity, security, and self-determination. Its members happily share bread with the hungry, but they also delight in helping the hungry set up communal farms and other enterprises so they can feed themselves. Members also work against despots to build community solidarity and create support programs that help marginalized populations voice their needs.

Abjurers of the Sheltering Hands also teach the rudiments of defensive magic to those who show interest and aptitude. Faction members who are mages lift curses and remove debilitating conditions; even members who can't cast the appropriate spells usually know enough to recognize what spells are needed.
Many of those the faction helps become members themselves, seeking to pay forward the support they've received and prevent others from suffering as they did.

entries.name: Balance of Faith
entries: The Sheltering Hands isn't a religious organization, though some of its members are priests and many venerate deities of mercy, charity, and self-sacrifice. The faction doesn't favor any particular religion and welcomes good-hearted members of all sorts, including former followers of evil faiths who have renounced their earlier affiliations. This nonsectarian policy allows the Sheltering Hands to coordinate relief or rescue efforts across organizations.

entries.name: Fieldwork
entries: Instead of expecting those in need to journey to them, small teams of Sheltering Hands members travel to deliver food, refresh supplies, and cast Abjuration spells. Spells from other schools of magic are often useful to repair structures, produce a bounty from sickly crops, or chase away opportunistic predators, so teams often include spellcasters with specialties other than Abjuration.

entries.name: Leadership and Organization

entries.title: Members of the Sheltering Hands cloak the vulnerable with protective magic.

entries: The faction's leadership council consists of five members. The council members make the hard decisions of allocating limited resources to do the most good.
The Leadership Council table presents the members of the faction's leadership council. All are Lawful Good.

entries.caption: Leadership Council
rows: Elbeezar (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM}), a human, comes from a farming village that supplies the faction's soup kitchens.
Nylusk (Medium {@creature Mage|XMM}), an orc, proudly walks with a limp earned while breaking up a riot.
Opener-of-Thought is a {@creature Deva|XMM} who prefers the form of a placid orangutan.
Slade (Medium {@creature Archpriest|XMM}), who is a human, believes the organization should put more resources into helping communities form long-term solutions.
Zosh (Small {@creature Mage|XMM}), a halfling, believes the organization should focus on providing emergency aid rather than pursuing long-term solutions.

entries.name: Dueling Priorities
entries: Friction within the Sheltering Hands comes from disagreements about how the organization might best help those in need. Some members believe the Sheltering Hands should focus on providing emergency aid to those experiencing hardship. Others believe that while providing aid is important, the organization should focus more on providing resources to communities to address societal struggles that cause long-term suffering. Some tension exists between these two groups, each of whose members believe their priority is superior. This dispute was minor at first, but some Sheltering Hands members have started refusing to serve alongside those of the opposite group, throwing off the faction's carefully planned administration.

entries.name: Joining the Sheltering Hands
entries: The Sheltering Hands welcomes all recruits interested in aiding the faction's mission, whether by offering protection during a faction outing or providing spellcasting services.

entries.name: Andarin's Aegis
entries: Andarin's Aegis is a large academy located in the temple district of a bustling metropolis. The Sheltering Hands established the academy as a school where its members can learn more about Abjuration magic, but, consistent with Sheltering Hands impulses, it has been used when needed as a soup kitchen, an impromptu medical center, a veteran's service center, and a shelter for children without homes. Its students are eager to learn from those who use Abjuration magic to aid others.

Andarin was one of the faction's earliest council members. Centuries after his death, many members still cite his dedication to helping the unhoused, but fewer remember his innovative contributions to the corpus of Abjuration spells.

The academy's dean is Malvanar Lumblin (Medium, Neutral Good {@creature Aberrant Cultist|XMM}), a garrulous human who has reformed his wicked ways. Students hang on his words when he talks about the beholder cult he once served. Malvanar's expertise about the antimagic nature of beholder eyes has proven revolutionary to abjurative studies.

entries.name: Renown Rewards
entries: Characters gain renown with the Sheltering Hands by aiding communities in great need or completing faction missions. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Sheltering Hands Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

entries.caption: Sheltering Hands Renown
rows: The Sheltering Hands provides you with simple food and lodging anywhere members are providing it to others.

A Sheltering Hands member can cast {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} on you or an ally in any town or city where the faction operates. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.
The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the seers give you an Uncommon magic item from the Armor or Staff category.
The Sheltering Hands hides and protects any magical item you want to ensure remains out of the hands of evil.

If you or your companions are at risk of suffering from {@hazard dehydration|XPHB} or {@hazard malnutrition|XPHB} while within 5 miles of a town or city where the faction operates, faction members bring you enough food and water to meet your needs.

A Sheltering Hands member can cast the {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell on you or an ally in any town or city where the faction operates. This reward is free the first time you use it. On subsequent occasions, you must provide any Material components normally consumed by the spell.

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, faction members teach you to magically protect those you care for. You always have the {@spell Warding Bond|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
You receive a 20 percent discount on spellcasting services purchased from faction members.

Faction members openly share information with you. Additionally, you can arrange for an audience with the council members. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases.

entries: The selfless mission of the Sheltering Hands is close to my heart. I relish the times I can visit these friends and bolster their supportive magic with my own.

entries.name: Sheltering Hands Characters
entries: Anyone with the ability and inclination to serve others has a place in the Sheltering Hands. As members travel to places where help is most needed, stalwart warriors are just as valuable as priests and mages. Faction members work closely together, so cooperation and conviction are required.

entries.title: Members of the Sheltering Hands receive Healer's Kits to help those in need.

entries: The most welcome are {@class Cleric|XPHB}, {@class Fighter|XPHB}, {@class Monk|XPHB}, {@class Paladin|XPHB}, and {@class Wizard|XPHB} (especially those with the {@class Wizard|XPHB|Abjurer|Abjurer|XPHB} subclass). Characters with proficiency in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}, proficiency with an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}, or the {@background Acolyte|XPHB} or {@background Ward of the Sheltering Hands|AU} background are also welcome.

entries.name: Member Benefits
entries: If you're a member of the Sheltering Hands, you receive these benefits.

entries.name: Healer's Kits
entries: The Sheltering Hands gives you a {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB}. If you return a {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB} with no uses remaining, the Sheltering Hands gives you a new {@item Healer's Kit|XPHB}. Once you make this exchange, this benefit can't be used for 7 days.

entries.name: Trinket
entries: Roll on the {@item Sheltering Hands Trinket|AU|Sheltering Hands Trinkets} table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Sheltering Hands.

entries.name: Using This Faction
entries: The Sheltering Hands is a benevolent organization without hidden motives or sinister secrets. It can come to the aid of the characters if they're in need. Alternatively, the faction might ask the characters for help: Perhaps a protective ritual needs a rare ingredient, or a shipment of food and medicine requires dedicated guards.

You can involve the characters in faction rivalries between those who disagree about organizational priorities. Such conflicts can be compelling because both sides have good intentions and neither is a clear villain.

entries.name: Special Facility
entries: Members of the Sheltering Hands can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

data.name: Chapter 5: Magic Items

entries.title: A retired adventurer shows his grandchild the artifact he found long ago in a dragon's lair: {@item Queen Ehlissa's Marvelous Nightingale|AU}.

entries: This chapter describes magic items particularly suited for settings brimming with arcane power. It also presents rules for magic item evolution, allowing you to create magic items that grow in might as your characters do, and ready-made evolving magic items meant as special rewards.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: The Magic Items table lists the magic items in this section and whether they require {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, ordered by item rarity. These items use the magic item rules in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}. The descriptions that follow are presented in alphabetical order.
The multiverse teems with magic items, each imbued with a speck of Mystra's might. Isn't it grand to be stewards of that power?

entries.name: Evolving Magic Items
entries: Few experiences infuse players with more wonder than their characters finding exciting magic items. Characters often grow fond of magic items that have personal significance, such as items that remind them of a beloved companion or a heroic deed.

As characters grow in power, though, that fondness can turn to frustration. A level 1 character's beloved Uncommon item might no longer be as useful by the time that character reaches level 5. Eventually, the character might have a dilemma: abandon their favorite magic item in favor of one with less personal significance, or keep the favored item, potentially forgoing a mechanically stronger option.

The magic item evolution rules in this section allow you to grant a magic item additional properties and increase its rarity as characters become more powerful. With these tools, you can build narrative significance into your characters' magic items and enable the items to grow in power as the characters do. This section presents several ready-made evolving magic items and rules for evolving certain magic items from the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG} or other sources.

entries.name: When to Evolve Magic Items
entries: You decide when a magic item evolves. In general, a magic item evolves when a character's power level increases to the next tier of play. Treat this as a guideline, not a rule.

entries.name: Repeated Evolutions
entries: You can evolve a magic item multiple times. Each time you evolve it, the magic item retains its properties from its previous rarity (or rarities) and gains a property from its new rarity.
You can evolve a magic item before or after awarding it to a character. In either case, you can increase the item's rarity as the character gains power until its rarity becomes Legendary.

entries.name: Crafting Evolution
entries: You might also decide that characters can evolve their magic items using the rules for crafting magic items in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG|6|Crafting Magic Items}. If you allow this, the time required to evolve the item equals the difference between the time required to craft an item of the evolving item's new rarity and the time required to craft an item of its previous rarity. Likewise, the cost required is the difference between the cost to craft an item of the evolving item's new rarity and the cost to craft an item of its previous rarity. So evolving an Uncommon item (which requires 10 days and 200 GP to craft) into a Rare item (which requires 50 days and 2,000 GP to craft) requires 40 days and 1,800 GP in raw materials.

entries.name: Results of Evolution
entries: This section describes the results of magic item evolution.

entries.name: Name and Appearance
entries: Each item's name changes when it evolves, as noted for that type of evolving magic item. Its appearance also changes as it evolves.

entries.name: Rarity
entries: When a magic item evolves, its rarity increases to the next highest rarity: from Common to Uncommon, from Rare to Very Rare, and so forth. A Legendary magic item can't evolve.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: A magic item keeps its {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} requirement (or lack thereof) as it evolves. If a creature is attuned to a magic item when the item evolves, the creature retains its {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to that item.

entries.name: Cumulative Abilities
entries: When an evolving magic item evolves, it retains the properties described in its previous rarities and gains the properties described in its new rarity. If an evolving weapon grants a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, however, that bonus replaces any similar bonus granted by a lower rarity instead of being added to it. For instance, in "Ready-Made Evolving Magic Items," a {@item Keyholes Dagger|AU}'s bonus to attack and damage rolls is +1 when Uncommon, +2 when Rare, and +3 when Very Rare.

entries.name: Ready-Made Evolving Magic Items
entries: The ready-made evolving magic items presented in this section and listed in the Ready-Made Evolving Magic Items table are special rewards. You might award a Ranger a {@item Blossom Rod|AU}, for example, to reinforce the character's connection with nature, gradually increasing the rod's rarity to reward the Ranger for their heroics. Similarly, a Necromancer might receive a {@item Staff of Skulls|AU} as a gift if their mentor works with the Covenant of the Grave magical faction (see {@book chapter 4|AU|4|Covenant of the Grave}).
You can structure a campaign arc around one of these items—use it to point the characters toward adventures related to its narrative, similar to how you might use an Artifact.

entries.name: Ready-Made Evolving Item Names
entries: When referring to one of these items, use the word that corresponds with the item's rarity before its name. For example, an Uncommon {@item Blossom Rod|AU} is a {@item Budding Blossom Rod|AU}, a Rare one is a {@item Flowering Blossom Rod|AU}, and a Very Rare one is a {@item Somniferous Blossom Rod|AU}.

entries.name: Custom Evolving Magic Items
entries: You can use magic items from the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} as the basis for evolving magic items.
This section presents two methods for creating your own evolving magic items: simple evolution and complex evolution.

entries.name: Simple Evolution
entries: If a character has one of the magic items in the Simple Magic Item Evolution table, you can evolve that item as shown on the table. For example, a {@item +1 Longsword|XDMG} that evolves becomes a {@item +2 Longsword|XDMG}, and if it evolves again, it becomes a {@item +3 Longsword|XDMG}.

entries.title: An Arrow-Catching Shield That Has Evolved into a Regal Arrow-Catching Shield

entries.caption: Simple Magic Item Evolution
rows: {@item +1 Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG|Rod of the Pact Keeper (Uncommon)}
{@item +2 Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG|Rod of the Pact Keeper (Rare)}
{@item +2 Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG|Rod of the Pact Keeper (Rare)}
{@item +3 Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG|Rod of the Pact Keeper (Very Rare)}
{@item +3 Wand of the War Mage|XDMG|3 Wand of the War Mage}

entries.name: Complex Evolution
entries: Some magic items can grow in strength beyond increasing the bonuses they grant. By granting a magic item new and more powerful magical properties, you can create an evolving magic item that grows in exciting ways.

Using the rules in this section, you can evolve eligible magic items from the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}. At your discretion, items from other sources might be eligible for evolution using these rules.
The following magic items are eligible for complex evolution:

items.name: Certain Rods and Wands:
items.entry: Any {@item Rod of the Pact Keeper|XDMG} or {@item Wand of the War Mage|XDMG}

items.name: Certain Other Uncommon or Rarer Magic Items:
items.entry: Any Armor, Staff, or Weapon that requires {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, that isn't cursed, and whose rarity is at most Very Rare

entries.name: Complex Evolution Steps
entries: To evolve an item with this system, use the following steps in conjunction with the instructions from "When to Evolve Magic Items" earlier in this chapter:

items.name: 1: Choose a Magic Item to Evolve
items.entry: Pick the eligible magic item you plan to evolve, and note its current rarity.

items.name: 2: Determine the Item's New Rarity
items.entry: The item's new rarity is the next highest rarity.

items.name: 3: Roll on or Choose from the New Rarity's Table
items.entry: Use the {@book Magic Item Properties table|AU|5|Rare Magic Item Properties} for the item's new rarity to select a new property, noting any details such as limited usage. (If the magic item grants a bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}, attack and damage rolls, saving throws, or spell save DCs, don't increase the bonus as part of evolving the item with this system. For example, if you evolve a {@item +1 Wand of the War Mage|XDMG} and give it a new property from this system, the item's bonus remains +1.)

items.name: 4: Determine the Item's New Name and Physical Characteristics
entries: Change the evolved item's name to represent its newfound power. If you like, you can give the item a new, more dramatic name. Either way, preface its name with the name of the property it just gained. For example, if you evolve a {@item Sword of Sharpness|XDMG} to be Legendary and grant it the Prismatic property, it would be called a Prismatic Sword of Sharpness.
Evolution also causes physical changes; examples include the appearance of magical runes or additional filigree.

entries.name: Magic Item Property Tables
entries: Roll on or choose from the tables that follow when determining new properties for complex evolving magic items.

entries.caption: Rare Magic Item Properties
rows: Amicable. When you fail an ability check made to influence a creature while holding or wearing this item, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success. This property can be used three times, and the item regains expended uses of this property daily at dawn.
Conversational. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Tongues|XPHB} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Crusading. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Crusader's Mantle|XPHB} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.
Displacing. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Blur|XPHB} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Frightening. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Fear|XPHB} (save {@dc 15}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Fulminating. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Lightning Bolt|XPHB} (save {@dc 15}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Immolating. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Fireball|XPHB} (save {@dc 15}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Quickening. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while holding or wearing this item, you can infuse yourself with magical velocity for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends. While you are infused, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled, and {@action opportunity attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Restorative. While holding or wearing this item, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast both {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} and {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB}, targeting the same creature. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Skulking. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Pass without Trace|XPHB|Pass Without A Trace} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Studious. When you fail an ability check made as part of the {@action Study|XPHB} action while holding or wearing this item, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success. This property can be used three times, and the item regains expended uses of this property daily at dawn.
Vigilant. While holding or wearing this item, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

entries: Some magic items are far more special than the wondrous trinkets you would find in a shop. Your parent's sword or your mentor's wand—hold these close and shut your eyes. That's when you'll feel their power.

entries.caption: Very Rare Magic Item Properties
rows: Chilling. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Deceptive. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Mislead|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Far-Seeing. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Scrying|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Fortunate. While attuned to this magic item, you can reroll one failed {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, and you must used the second roll. This property can be used twice, and the item regains expended uses of this property daily at dawn.

Lunar. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Fount of Moonlight|XPHB} or {@spell Moonbeam|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

Paralyzing. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Hold Monster|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Psionic. While holding or wearing this item, you have telepathy with a range of 30 feet, and you can cast {@spell Synaptic Static|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Regal. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Yolande's Regal Presence|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Resilient. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Otiluke's Resilient Sphere|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Resistant. While attuned to this item, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one of the following damage types (DM's choice): Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder.

Traversing. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Dimension Door|XPHB} or {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB} from it. Once the item has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

Withering. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Blight|XPHB} or {@spell Vampiric Touch|XPHB} (save {@dc 17}, +9 to hit with spell attacks) from it. Once the item has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

entries.caption: Legendary Magic Item Properties
rows: All-Seeing. While attuned to this item, you have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.
Empowering. While attuned to this item, one of your ability scores (DM's choice) increases by 2, to a maximum of 24.

Gravitational. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Reverse Gravity|XPHB} (save {@dc 18}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Heliacal. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Sunburst|XPHB} (save {@dc 18}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Prismatic. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Prismatic Spray|XPHB} (save {@dc 18}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.
Spellguarding. While holding or wearing this item, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Stupefying. While holding or wearing this item, you can cast {@spell Power Word Stun|XPHB} (save {@dc 18}) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.
